2.0The five things that are true of every treatment

No session starts until all five are done and recorded. Missing documentation is a clinical compliance failure and is reported to the Branch Manager the same day.

Baseline protocol
#Baseline stepWhat it means in practice
1Medical clearanceScreen for pregnancy, lactation, active malignancy, liver or kidney disease, pacemakers, and active wounds or infection in the target area. Any confirmed contraindication = do not proceed without Medical Head approval.
2Body metricsRecord weight, BMI and a body composition analysis where the treatment is body-related. Baseline waist, hip, abdomen and thigh measurements as applicable.
3Standardised photography4-angle photographs — anterior, posterior, left lateral, right lateral — in fixed lighting with consistent positioning. Stored in the ERP record immediately.
4Informed consentSigned, treatment-specific consent. Explain expected outcomes, number of sessions, risks, side effects and post-care requirements.
5Treatment plan sign-offA valid, current doctor's treatment plan on file. No therapist may proceed without it.

3.0How to use this document

Before a session

Open the treatment page. Read the eligible / not-eligible panel and the red flag list. If anything on the right-hand column is present, stop and call the CM or dermatologist. The search box takes a treatment name, a brand name, a machine or a body area.

During a session

The parameter tables and the numbered protocol are the working reference. The ‘watch continuously’ block lists what makes you stop mid-treatment — those are not warnings, they are instructions.

After a session

Print the matching handout, fill in the footer, hand it over and read the ‘call us if’ section aloud. Then log the session in ERP before the client leaves the branch.

What is LIFE

RECHARGE YOUR LIFE · Slimming | Hair | Skin | Laser

LIFE Slimming and Cosmetic Clinic Pvt. Ltd. is a multi-branch aesthetic and wellness clinic group operating across Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. We bring dermatology, body contouring, trichology, hair transplant surgery and clinical nutrition together under one roof, delivered to a single written standard at every branch.

1.0What we stand for

One standard, every branch

Every treatment in this Knowledge Centre runs to a written SOP. A client walking into Nellore gets the same protocol as a client in Banjara Hills — same screening, same parameters, same aftercare.

Doctor-led, therapist-delivered

Clinical decisions belong to the doctor. Delivery belongs to trained, certified therapists. The line between the two is written down for every treatment, not left to judgement on the day.

Documented or it did not happen

Every session is logged in ERP before the client leaves. Consent, parameters, skin response and adverse events. This protects the client, the therapist and the clinic.

Say no when the answer is no

Screening exists to be acted on. A therapist who stops a treatment because of a contraindication has done their job correctly, even if it costs a session.

4.0The ten questions that catch most problems

  • Are you pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning a pregnancy?
  • Have you taken Roaccutane or any acne tablet in the last 6 months?
  • Do you have a pacemaker, metal plate, screw, or a copper IUD?
  • Any laser, peel, filler, Botox or microneedling in the last 4 weeks?
  • Sun, sunbed or self-tan in the last 4 weeks?
  • Have you ever had a cold sore — anywhere, ever?
  • What medicines, supplements or herbal products are you taking right now?
  • Any surgery in this area in the last 3 to 6 months?
  • Do you scar badly, or have you ever had a keloid?
  • Has anything changed since your last session — illness, medication, diagnosis?
Ask, do not assumeScreening happens before every session, not only at the first visit. Pregnancy, medication and recent procedures change between appointments, and clients do not volunteer them.
Screening & safety

Red flags & escalation

What stops a treatment, who you call, and how fast.

Stopping a treatment is never a mistake. Continuing one you should have stopped is. Nobody at LIFE is disciplined for stopping a session over a safety concern.

1.0Severity grades

Graded response
GradeWhat it coversRequired response
P1 — CriticalAnaphylaxis · vascular occlusion · vision change after filler · loss of consciousness · suspected malignancy missedSTOP. Emergency services (108) if indicated. Doctor at the chair. Call CM, then COO, immediately. Do not leave the client. Log within 1 hour.
P2 — SeriousBurns and blisters · deep tissue injury · infection · nerve symptoms · thread extrusion · depigmentationSTOP. First aid. Photograph. Call CM; CM calls COO. Tag the machine out of service if machine-related. CIRF within 4 hours.
P3 — ModerateProlonged redness · PIH · allergic reaction to product · vasovagal episode · asymmetryStop the session. Doctor or dermatologist review. Document in ERP the same day. Notify CM.
P4 — MinorExpected redness · follicular oedema · pinpoint crusting · normal post-treatment sorenessReassure with the expected timeline. Standard aftercare. Document in ERP.

2.0Before treatment — do not begin

Stop at the chair

  • Consent form for this session is not signed
  • Visible active herpes, cold sore or blister anywhere on the face
  • Fresh sunburn, tan with redness, or hot skin over the area
  • Isotretinoin within the last 6 months
  • Open acne pustules, cysts or weeping lesions in the area
  • Client visibly unwell, feverish, or with flu-like symptoms
  • Pregnancy, suspected pregnancy or breastfeeding disclosed
  • Laser, peel or IPL in the same area within 4 weeks
  • Pacemaker, metal implant or copper IUD disclosed
  • Skin unusually thin, fragile, or showing steroid atrophy
  • Client cannot feel heat or sensation normally in the area
  • Any pigmented lesion in the field that has recently changed, bled or itched

3.0During treatment — stop immediately

Stop mid-session

  • Sharp, burning or stinging pain beyond mild warmth
  • Blanching, whitening or mottling that is not the expected endpoint
  • Immediate blistering, skin lifting or tissue damage
  • Sudden redness, hives or swelling suggesting allergy
  • Client feels dizzy, nauseous, or loses consciousness
  • Abnormal burning-skin odour
  • Machine firing inconsistently, error codes, or unexpected energy
  • Eye protection dislodging during any laser treatment
  • Skin surface above 44°C on any RF device
  • Facial twitching or radiating pain during HIFU or thread placement
  • The client asks you to stop — for any reason, honour it immediately

4.0After treatment — recall the client

Act the same day

  • Blistering, peeling or an open wound within 30 minutes
  • Severe or prolonged redness or swelling beyond 2 hours
  • Paradoxical darkening of pigment immediately after Q-Switch
  • White patches or depigmentation appearing after treatment
  • Extreme pain, burning or sensitivity on leaving
  • Infection signs within 24–48 hours — pus, heat, spreading redness, fever
  • Herpes outbreak after treatment
  • Increasing pain, colour change or any visual symptom after filler — emergency
  • Painless firm enlargement of a cryolipolysis-treated area at 3–6 months

5.0Emergency response by event

What to do, in order
EventImmediate action
Thermal or freeze burnStop. Cold saline compress — never ice directly. Silver sulfadiazine or burn ointment. Doctor now. Log in ERP. Do not resume.
Vascular occlusion after fillerStop. Flood with hyaluronidase per protocol. Warm compress, massage, aspirin per protocol. Escalate to Medical Head and COO immediately. Hourly review.
Vision change or eye pain after fillerOphthalmic emergency. Call 108. Immediate ophthalmology referral. Notify Medical Head and COO.
AnaphylaxisStop everything. Adrenaline per protocol. Call 108. Oxygen. Doctor manages. Do not leave the client. Notify within 1 hour.
Vasovagal episodeLay flat, elevate legs, check BP and pulse. Recovery time. Do not resume same day. Log in ERP.
Nodules or necrosis after injection lipolysisImmediate physician evaluation. Do not massage. Physician decides steroid or hyaluronidase. Log in ERP.
Paradoxical Adipose Hyperplasia after cryoLog as PAH. Cease all further cryo to that area. Refer to plastic surgeon. Notify Medical Head and COO.
Suspected missed malignancyUrgent dermatology referral. Escalate to Medical Head and COO. Preserve all photographs and records.
Critical incident protocolEvery adverse event is logged in ERP within 1 hour and escalated to the Medical Head and COO the same day. Photograph the area. Tag the machine out of service if machine-related. CIRF within 4 hours. This is not negotiable at branch level.

You have the right to be fully informed about the recommended procedure so that you can make an informed decision whether or not to proceed. This disclosure is not intended to alarm you; it is to ensure you can give or withhold your informed consent.

1   Overview of the procedure

Cryolipolysis uses controlled cooling to reduce localised pockets of fat. It is a body contouring treatment, not a weight loss treatment. Results develop gradually and peak 8 to 12 weeks after treatment.

2   Possible side effects and risks

  • Redness, swelling, bruising, tenderness and firmness in the treated area.
  • Numbness or tingling in the treated area, which may last several weeks.
  • Cramping or aching during and shortly after the treatment.
  • Rarely, freeze burn or blistering of the skin.
  • Rarely, Paradoxical Adipose Hyperplasia — a firm enlargement of the treated fat in the shape of the applicator, appearing 3 to 6 months later, which may require surgical correction.
  • Results vary between individuals. More than one session may be required.

GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy is a prescription medical treatment for weight management. It works alongside — not instead of — a structured nutrition and exercise plan, and requires monthly medical review.

  • Increased risk of aspiration during anaesthesia — this drug must be declared before any surgery.
  • Weight regain after stopping if lifestyle change is not maintained.
  • This medication is not suitable in pregnancy and must be stopped before conception.

Body Contouring — Before & After Your Session
Cryolipolysis · NSLS · RF Body · HIFU Body · EMS · Drainage · Wraps
HO-BODY
Before your treatment
  • Drink at least 2 litres of water in the 24 hours before your session — this is not optional. Cavitation and drainage do not work properly on a dehydrated body.
  • Eat a light meal at least 2 hours before. Do not come on a completely empty stomach or straight after a heavy meal.
  • No alcohol for 24 hours before your session.
  • Come with clean skin. No body lotion, oil, sunscreen or perfume on the treatment area.
  • Remove all jewellery from and near the treatment area.
  • Wear loose, comfortable clothing.
  • Tell us before we start if anything has changed — new medication, pregnancy, surgery, a new medical diagnosis, or a pacemaker or implant.
After your treatment
  • Drink 2.5 to 3 litres of water every day for the next 4 days. This is how your body clears the treated fat.
  • Walk briskly or do light cardio for 20 to 30 minutes within 4 to 6 hours of your session.
  • Massage the treated area gently for 5 minutes daily for 7 days after cavitation or cryolipolysis.
  • Eat lightly for 24 hours — no heavy, fried or very rich meals.
  • Mild redness, warmth, numbness or tenderness is normal and settles within a few hours to a few days.
Please avoid
  • No alcohol for 72 hours. Alcohol competes with fat clearance in your liver and will reduce your result.
  • No heavy refined carbohydrates or sugar for 72 hours.
  • No hot shower, sauna, steam room or hot tub for 48 hours.
  • No heavy body creams, oils or heat products on the treated area for 24 hours.
Call the clinic straight away if you notice
  • Blistering, or skin that changes colour
  • Pain that gets worse instead of better after 24 hours
  • Swelling that is still increasing after 48 hours
  • A firm, painless enlargement of a cryolipolysis-treated area 3 to 6 months later

Hair Transplant — Your Complete Recovery Guide
FUE Hair Transplant — pre-operative and post-operative
HO-HT
Before your treatment
  • Stop smoking 2 weeks before surgery. Smoking directly reduces how many grafts survive.
  • No alcohol for 3 days before.
  • Stop any blood-thinning medication only as instructed by your surgeon — never stop it on your own.
  • Wash your hair the morning of surgery with the shampoo provided.
  • Eat a normal breakfast on the day.
  • Wear a shirt that buttons at the front — you must not pull clothing over your head afterwards.
  • Arrange for someone to take you home.
After your treatment
  • Sleep with your head raised at 45 degrees for the first 7 nights.
  • Attend the Day 1 supervised wash — do not attempt the first wash alone.
  • From Day 2, wash exactly as we demonstrated: gentle pouring, no rubbing, no direct shower pressure.
  • Take all medication as prescribed — antibiotics, anti-inflammatories and painkillers.
  • Swelling of the forehead around Day 2 to 4 is normal and settles by itself.
  • The transplanted hair WILL fall out at 2 to 4 weeks. This is expected and is not a failure.
  • Regrowth begins at 3 to 4 months. The final result is at 12 to 18 months.
  • Keep taking the medication prescribed to protect your existing hair.
Please avoid
  • Do not touch, scratch or pick the grafts or scabs.
  • Nothing on your head — no cap, helmet or towel pressure — for 7 days unless we tell you otherwise.
  • No smoking for 2 weeks after.
  • No alcohol for 1 week.
  • No gym, swimming, sauna or heavy sweating for 3 weeks.
  • No direct sun on the scalp for 4 weeks.
  • No hair colour or chemical treatment for 4 weeks.
  • Do not sleep face-down.
Call the clinic straight away if you notice
  • Fever
  • Spreading redness or pus from the donor or recipient area
  • Bleeding that does not stop with 10 minutes of gentle pressure
  • Severe pain not controlled by your prescribed painkiller

GLP-1 Weight Management — Your Programme Guide
Semaglutide · Tirzepatide
HO-GLP1
Before your treatment
  • Complete your blood tests before your first dose — HbA1c, kidney function and liver function.
  • Tell the doctor about every medication and supplement you take.
  • Tell us if anyone in your family has had thyroid cancer.
  • Tell us if you have ever had pancreatitis or gallbladder problems.
  • Plan your protein sources before you start — this is the single most important thing you can do.
After your treatment
  • Inject on the same day each week. Rotate the injection site.
  • Store your pen in the fridge at 2 to 8°C. Do not freeze it.
  • Eat a minimum of 60 to 80 g of protein every day. Losing muscle instead of fat is the main risk of this treatment.
  • Eat small, slow meals. Stop at the first feeling of fullness.
  • Do at least 150 minutes of exercise a week, and include strength training.
  • Attend every monthly review. The dose is only increased when the current one is well tolerated.
  • Tell any doctor, surgeon or dentist that you are on this medication before any procedure.
Please avoid
  • Do not increase your dose yourself.
  • Do not skip meals to lose faster — you will lose muscle.
  • Avoid large, fatty or fried meals — they make nausea much worse.
  • Avoid alcohol, which worsens nausea and low blood sugar.
  • Do not continue this medication if you are planning a pregnancy — speak to the doctor first.
Call the clinic straight away if you notice
  • Severe abdominal pain, especially going through to your back — this could be pancreatitis and needs urgent attention
  • Pain under your right ribs — this could be your gallbladder
  • Persistent vomiting or inability to keep fluids down
  • Any planned surgery or procedure — tell us before you book it

Theory — understood, not memorised
  • Skin anatomy and the hair growth cycle — anagen, catagen, telogen, and why only anagen hairs respond
  • Fitzpatrick skin typing — how to assess it correctly, not guess it
  • Selective photothermolysis: wavelength, fluence, pulse width and how each affects safety
  • The full contraindication list and why each one is on it

  • Post-treatment application and gel removal without abrasion

  • 10 supervised sessions covering at least 3 different body areas and at least 2 skin types above Fitzpatrick III
  • Trainer observes and corrects in real time; therapist documents each session in ERP under supervision
Assessment

  • Practical assessment: full session start to finish, observed and scored
  • Verbal viva: 'A client arrives with a fresh tan and no patch test. Walk me through what you do.'

Cryolipolysis (Fat Freezing)

4D Cryo · CoolSculpting · 3D Cryo · Fat Freeze
Session time35–60 min per probe cycleCourse1–2 sessions per areaIntervalEvery 6–8 weeks per target areaResults seenVisible at 8–12 weeks post-treatmentPerformed byTrained therapist · Doctor clearance mandatory

1.0What this treatment is

A non-invasive fat reduction treatment that uses controlled cooling to freeze and permanently destroy fat cells in a targeted area, without damaging skin, nerves or surrounding tissue.

The mechanism

Controlled cooling to −5°C to −10°C triggers apoptosis (natural cell death) in adipocytes. The destroyed fat cells are cleared by the lymphatic system over 4–12 weeks. This reduces the localised fat bulge permanently — it is body contouring, not weight loss.

Equipment used

4D Cryo Machine · CoolSculpting · Zimmer (skin cooling)

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-CRYO-001 · SOP-SLM-001 §2A · SOP-SLM-002 P1

2.0What it treats

  • Localised, pinchable subcutaneous fat pockets
  • Upper and lower abdomen
  • Flanks / love handles
  • Inner and outer thighs (saddle bags)
  • Back fat / bra bulge
  • Submental fat (double chin)
  • Banana roll (under-buttock fold)
  • Upper arm fat

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+ years
  • BMI. Generally below 35 — not for obese clients
  • Fat type. Pinchable subcutaneous fat, minimum 2–3 cm in the pinch test
  • Skin. Good elasticity, intact, no infection or wound in area
  • Weight status. Stable weight — not rapidly gaining or losing
  • Expectations. Understands this is fat reduction, not weight loss
  • Clearance. Doctor has cleared the client for the procedure

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Cryoglobulinaemia, cold agglutinin disease, paroxysmal cold haemoglobinuria
  • Raynaud's disease or known cold hypersensitivity / cold urticaria
  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Active skin infection, open wounds or rashes in the treatment area
  • Hernia in the treatment area
  • Implanted devices (pacemaker, metal implants) near the treatment area
  • Severe varicose veins in the treatment area
  • Neuropathy or loss of sensation in the treatment area
  • Recent surgery within 6 months in the treatment area
  • Chilblains or history of perniosis
  • Active cancer or malignancy
  • Uncontrolled diabetes (high or unstable blood sugar)

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • BMI above 35 — doctor assessment required, limited efficacy
  • Pinch fold under 2 cm — zone not suitable, document and inform doctor
  • History of keloid or hypertrophic scarring
  • Recent aesthetic injectable in the area within 4 weeks
  • Clients on anticoagulants — bruising risk
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Cooling temperature−5°C to −10°C (machine controlled)
Cycle timePer machine protocol — typically 35–50 min per probe
Probes per sessionAs per treatment plan; 1 gel membrane = maximum 2 probes
Minimum pinch2 cm fat fold — mandatory pinch test before every probe
Post-removal massage2 minutes, mandatory

5.0Step-by-step protocol

PRE-1
Verify client identity & consent
Check client ID against appointment. Confirm signed Cryo consent form is on file. Check medical-condition stickers on the client record card.
PRE-2
BP & blood sugar check
Check BP and blood sugar for hypertensive, diabetic and GLP-1 programme clients. Record in the Daily Vitals Register.
PRE-3
Room & machine preparation
Room clean, bed covered with clean sheet. Machine powered on and tested. Settings display confirmed working.
PRE-4
Membrane inventory check
Count gel membranes. Each membrane must carry 2 pre-assigned serial numbers written in the register BEFORE the session begins.
PRE-5
Explain the procedure
Explain cooling sensation, suction, numbness and post-treatment redness. Answer all questions before starting.
PRE-6
Client positioning
Position per target zone. Expose only the treatment area. Keep the rest of the body warm with a blanket.
PRE-7
Before photo
Clear before photo from standard angles — front, side, back where applicable. Store in the client record.
1
Skin preparation
Wipe the target area with the pre-treatment skin preparation wipe. Allow to dry.
2
Pinch test & marking
Client standing. Pinch the fat pocket to locate the centre. Confirm minimum 2 cm fold. Mark the pocket boundary and applicator centre with a skin marker.
3
Anti-freeze membrane
Apply the gel membrane flat against the skin with ZERO air bubbles — trapped air causes localised freeze burns. Record the membrane serial number in the register.
4
Applicator placement
Place the applicator on the tissue. Engage vacuum suction gently and progressively — never in one sudden pull. Fat bulge must fill the cup; no skin folds outside the cup edge.
5
Secure applicator
Secure so the weight of the machine cord cannot displace the cup during the cycle.
6
Session monitoring
Verify tissue temperature pull-down on the console. Monitor continuously. Moderate cold pain and numbness in the first 5–8 minutes is expected.
7
POST — 2-minute shock massage
MANDATORY immediately on applicator removal: 1 minute of vigorous knuckle kneading to crush the crystallised lipid walls, then 1 minute of firm circular pressure to restore blood flow. This raises fat-reduction efficacy by up to 68%. Skipping it significantly reduces the result.
8
Membrane disposal
After 2 probe uses the membrane is DISCARDED into biomedical waste. Never stored, folded for later, or used on another client.
9
Post-care & handout
Apply soothing cream. Give the client the printed post-care card. Book the next session.
10
ERP documentation
Log zone, probe, cycle time, membrane serial numbers, skin response and therapist name before the client leaves.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Severe ongoing pain beyond 8 minutes requires assessment — do not push through
  • Check skin colour at the cup edge — deep purple/white blanching outside the cup is abnormal
  • Client reports of burning rather than cold numbness = stop and assess

Before the client leaves the chair

  • 2-minute shock massage — non-negotiable
  • Apply soothing post-treatment cream
  • 10 minutes of light activity before the client leaves
  • Apply Fat Dissolving Solution (FDS) for 45 minutes post-session where prescribed

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Drink 2.5–3 litres of water daily for 4 days
  • 20–30 minutes of brisk walking within 4–6 hours of treatment
  • Daily 5-minute self-massage of the treated area for 7 days
  • Low-carbohydrate, low-fat diet for 72 hours
  • Expect numbness, tingling, redness and mild swelling for a few days — this is normal
  • Report any painless firm enlargement of the area at 3–6 months immediately

Avoid this

  • No alcohol for 72 hours — it competes with fat clearance in the liver
  • No heavy refined carbohydrates or sugar for 72 hours
  • No hot bath, sauna or steam for 48 hours
  • Do not expect instant results — peak result is at 8–12 weeks
  • Do not book a repeat on the same area before 6 weeks

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Redness, numbness, tinglingMinor (P4)Normal response. Reassure. Resolves over hours to days. Document.
Freeze burn / blisteringSerious (P2)Stop. Cold saline compress — never ice directly on skin. Silver sulfadiazine or clinical burn ointment. Call doctor + CM immediately. Tag machine OOS. Log in ERP within 1 hour.
Vasovagal episode / faintingModerate (P3)Lay flat, elevate legs, check BP and pulse. Allow recovery. Do not resume the same day. Log in ERP.
Paradoxical Adipose Hyperplasia (PAH)Serious (P2)Client returns at 3–6 months with painless, firm 'butter-stick' enlargement in the exact applicator shape. Log as PAH in ERP. Cease all further cryo to that area. Refer to plastic surgeon. Notify Medical Head and COO.
Prolonged pain beyond 2 weeksModerate (P3)Doctor review. Do not retreat until resolved. Document.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • No signed consent on file — do not start
  • Pinch fold under 2 cm in the intended zone
  • Membrane without a recorded serial number
  • Air bubble visible under the membrane after probe placement
  • Client discloses cold hypersensitivity, Raynaud's, or a hernia at the chair
  • Skin outside the cup edge blanching white during the cycle

NSLS — Non-Surgical Liposuction (Cavitation + RF)

Ultrasound Cavitation + Radiofrequency · Non-Surgical Lipo
Session time15–45 min depending on body area (see parameter table)Course6–10 sessions per areaIntervalEvery 5–7 days (7–10 days for face/jowls)Results seenInitial inch loss after 3–4 sessions; full result 6–8 weeks after the coursePerformed byTrained & certified NSLS therapist

1.0What this treatment is

A two-stage non-invasive body contouring treatment. Ultrasound cavitation ruptures fat cell membranes; radiofrequency then tightens the skin over the treated area in the same session.

The mechanism

Cavitation uses 40 kHz ultrasound to create micro-bubbles in the fluid around adipocytes. The bubbles implode, rupturing the fat cell membrane without damaging nerves, vessels or connective tissue. Released fatty acids and glycerol are cleared through the lymphatic system. RF then delivers controlled electrical energy that heats the dermis to 40–45°C, contracting existing collagen immediately and stimulating new collagen and elastin over weeks.

Equipment used

Cavitation + RF combination unit (40 kHz body / 1 MHz chin head)

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-NSLS-001 · SOP-SLM-001 §2C/2D · SOP-SLM-002 P3/P4

2.0What it treats

  • Localised stubborn fat that does not respond to diet and exercise
  • Abdomen, flanks and love handles
  • Thighs (inner and outer)
  • Upper arms
  • Upper and lower back / bra fat
  • Buttocks contouring
  • Gynaecomastia (male chest) — low intensity
  • Double chin (1 MHz head only)
  • Facial contouring and jowls — RF ONLY

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18 to 65 years. Above 65 with dermatologist clearance
  • BMI. 22–38 for best results; up to 40 with dermatologist clearance
  • Fat type. Localised, pinchable subcutaneous fat — not visceral fat
  • Skin. Intact, no active infection, wound or rash in the area
  • Hydration. Minimum 2 litres of water before the session
  • Expectations. Progressive results over 6–10 sessions. Not an instant result
  • Lifestyle. Willing to maintain a healthy diet and light exercise

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pacemaker, cardiac defibrillator or any implanted electronic stimulation device
  • Metal implants, surgical plates, pins, screws or rods in or near the area
  • Cochlear implants or any active implanted medical device
  • IUD in place — do not treat abdomen / pelvic area
  • Pregnancy (any trimester), suspected pregnancy, or breastfeeding
  • Active cancer, on chemotherapy or radiotherapy, or cancer history in the treatment area
  • DVT, pulmonary embolism or active clotting disorder
  • Severe uncontrolled hypertension (systolic above 180 mmHg)
  • Severe uncontrolled heart disease or cardiac event within 6 months
  • Active liver disease or liver failure — the body cannot process released lipids
  • Active kidney disease or renal failure
  • Active epilepsy or sound/vibration-triggered seizures
  • Active autoimmune conditions: Lupus, Scleroderma, Dermatomyositis
  • Active severe skin infection, open wounds, ulcers or acute inflammation in the area
  • Active herpes outbreak in the treatment area
  • Blood-borne disease with active liver involvement
  • Any surgery in the treatment area within 3 months; liposuction within 6 months
  • Any filler or fat-dissolving injectable in the area within 4 weeks
  • Under 18 years — no exceptions
  • Unable to give informed consent
  • Alcohol consumed within 24 hours
  • Known allergy to ultrasound or RF coupling gel

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Poorly controlled Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes — sugar must be in range on the day
  • Thyroid disorders — especially when treating neck or chin
  • History of keloid or hypertrophic scarring
  • Psoriasis, vitiligo or eczema in or near the treatment area
  • Peripheral neuropathy — client cannot report heat accurately
  • Immunosuppression from steroids or immunosuppressants
  • Severe anaemia or haematological conditions
  • History of thrombophlebitis
  • PCOS with active hormonal imbalance — results may be limited
  • BMI above 40 — dermatologist assessment; limited efficacy
  • Very thin skin, compromised skin integrity, or prior radiation to the area
  • Anticoagulants: Warfarin, Heparin, long-term Aspirin
  • Photosensitising medication; long-term high-dose corticosteroids
  • Isotretinoin within the last 6 months
  • Hormonal therapy / HRT affecting fat distribution
  • Diuretics — hydration monitoring required
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Client verification
Confirm name, ID, session number and treatment area against ERP and the treatment file.
2
Consent check
Confirm the signed consent form is in the file for this session.
3
Pre-treatment assessment
Inspect the area for skin issues, wounds or redness. If found, stop and consult CM or dermatologist.
4
Measurements
Sessions 1, 4 and 8: take body measurements in cm and photograph. Update ERP.
5
Hydration check
Confirm the client has had at least 2 litres of water today. If not, have them drink before starting.
6
Area cleansing
Cleanse with a gentle cleanser. Remove all product residue. Pat dry completely.
7
Apply ultrasound gel
Generous, even layer over the full treatment area.
8
Set cavitation parameters
40 kHz body / 1 MHz chin. Intensity per the area table. NEVER use cavitation on the face.
9
Cavitation delivery
Slow, overlapping circular or linear strokes. Firm skin contact at all times. Cover the area methodically. Angle the probe toward the fat fold, never flat over bone or organs.
10
Cavitation timing
Treat for the prescribed time using a timer. Do not overtreat.
11
Client check
Ringing in the ears is normal (bone conduction). Check comfort every 3–5 minutes. Reduce intensity on discomfort.
12
Remove cavitation gel
Wipe with a clean soft towel. Do not rub aggressively.
13
Apply RF coupling gel
RF conductive gel or coupling cream over the same area.
14
Set RF parameters
Per the area table. Start at the lower end and build up on skin temperature and client tolerance.
15
RF delivery
Slow circular strokes, constant movement. NEVER hold static on one spot.
16
Temperature monitoring
Target 40–42°C surface. Check every 2 minutes with the built-in sensor or IR thermometer. STOP at 45°C.
17
RF timing
Prescribed RF time per area. Use a timer.
18
Remove RF gel
Gently remove, pat dry.
19
Post-treatment application
Soothing lotion or prescribed post-treatment cream.
20
Lymphatic drainage massage
5–10 minutes of gentle manual drainage toward the nearest node cluster — groin for lower body, axilla for upper abdomen and torso.
21
Client instructions
Verbal plus written post-treatment card before the client leaves.
22
ERP documentation
Area, parameters, skin response, measurements where applicable.
23
Machine care
Clean handpieces with the recommended solution. Power down per manufacturer instructions.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Never hold the cavitation transducer stationary — acoustic energy concentrates and causes internal thermal burns
  • Never angle the transducer toward intestines, kidneys, uterus or bone
  • Skin surface above 44–45°C on RF: lift the probe, increase handpiece speed, apply cooling gel
  • Client reporting sharp burning rather than warmth = reduce power immediately

Before the client leaves the chair

  • 5–10 minutes manual lymphatic drainage

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Drink at least 2 litres of water after the session and for 48 hours — critical for lymphatic clearance
  • Light exercise (walking, cycling) within 24 hours
  • Eat light and clean for 24 hours
  • Report persistent redness, swelling beyond 24 hours, blistering or pain immediately

Avoid this

  • No alcohol for 48–72 hours — it blocks the liver from processing released lipids
  • No heavy, fatty or processed meals for 24 hours
  • No hot shower, sauna or steam room for 24 hours
  • No heavy body creams, oils or heat-based products on the area for 24 hours

1
Pre-execution checklist
Verify no metal implants, plates, screws or fixators. Confirm no copper IUD for abdominal work. Remove all jewellery and piercings. Confirm no active skin conditions, burns or recent procedures. Confirm no pacemaker.
2
Coupling medium
Apply the recommended coupling medium evenly — ultrasound gel for thermal RF, or pure glycerin where the gel evaporates too fast under high heat.
3
Handpiece motion
Move continuously in rapid, overlapping circular motions. Build heat gradually to 40–43°C.
4
Therapeutic window
Hold 40–43°C for 10–15 minutes per zone. This is the window that remodels collagen.
5
Temperature monitoring
Check every 2 minutes with the built-in thermal sensor or an external IR thermometer.
6
Thermal burn prevention
Above 44°C: lift the probe away, increase handpiece speed, apply cooling gel. Do NOT continue at elevated temperature.
7
Post-treatment
Remove gel, apply soothing lotion, brief the client, document parameters in ERP.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Never hold the handpiece static
  • Temperature above 44°C causes thermal burns and permanent scarring
  • Client reporting sharp pain rather than deep warmth = reduce power

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Soothing lotion
  • Lymphatic drainage strokes where combined with cavitation
  • Brief on heat avoidance

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Drink 2.5 litres of water daily for 4 days
  • Light activity same day
  • Expect mild redness and warmth for 1–2 hours

Avoid this

  • No hot bath, sauna or steam for 48 hours
  • No alcohol for 48 hours
  • No heat-based products on the area for 24 hours

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Mild erythemaMinor (P4)Normal. Cool towel. Monitor.
Thermal burn / blisterSerious (P2)Stop. Cold saline compress — never ice directly. Silver sulfadiazine or burn ointment. Call doctor + CM. Tag machine OOS. Log within 1 hour.
Prolonged redness beyond 24 hoursModerate (P3)Doctor review. Reduce power for future sessions. Document.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Metal implant or pacemaker disclosed at the chair
  • Copper IUD with planned abdominal treatment
  • Temperature reading above 44°C
  • Client cannot feel the heat (neuropathy)

HIFU Body

High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound — Body
Session time45–75 minutes depending on areaCourse1–3 sessionsIntervalEvery 8–12 weeksResults seen8–12 weeksPerformed byTrained therapist · doctor on site

1.0What this treatment is

Focused ultrasound energy delivered at fixed depths to disrupt deep structural fat and tighten the fascial (SMAS) layer without breaking the skin.

The mechanism

Ultrasound energy is focused at a precise depth, raising tissue temperature at that focal point to a coagulation threshold while leaving the skin surface untouched. This destroys deep adipocytes and triggers fascial contraction and collagen remodelling.

Equipment used

HIFU platform with 8.0 mm and 13.0 mm body transducers

Reference SOP

SOP-SLM-001 §2E · SOP-SLM-002 P5

2.0What it treats

  • Deep structural fat that does not respond to cavitation
  • Abdomen and tummy
  • Jawline, arms, thighs
  • Fascial (SMAS) tightening on the body

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Fat thickness. Minimum 2.5 cm subcutaneous fat, verified with a caliper
  • Skin. Intact, no infection or wound
  • Metal. No implants in the treatment area
  • Devices. No pacemaker or implanted electronic device

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or lactation
  • Cardiac pacemaker or implanted electronic device
  • Metal implants in the treatment area
  • Active cancer or malignancy
  • Severe hepatic or renal impairment
  • Hernia in the target area
  • Recent surgery in the area within 3 months
  • Severe varicose veins in the area
  • Active skin infection or open wounds in the area

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Subcutaneous fat under 2.5 cm — not suitable, document and inform the doctor
  • Keloid history
  • Neuropathy in the area
  • Uncontrolled diabetes
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Cartridge depth — body8.0 mm (subcutaneous fat) · 13.0 mm (deep fat / fascial)
Shot spacingParallel linear grids, 5 mm apart
Minimum fat thickness2.5 cm, caliper verified
Exclusion zonesAbdominal midline (linea alba), umbilicus, all major nerve pathways
Shot countLogged per cartridge per patient in ERP before and after every session

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Map the treatment area
Mark boundaries on the skin before starting.
2
Mark exclusion zones
Midline of the abdomen (linea alba), the umbilicus, and all identified major nerve pathways.
3
Cartridge selection
8.0 mm for subcutaneous fat, 13.0 mm for deep fat and fascial layers. NEVER use face cartridges on the body.
4
Shot count check
Check and log the remaining shot count on each cartridge in ERP before beginning.
5
Gel application
Standard ultrasound gel, full and even coverage.
6
Transducer contact
Place firmly, 100% flat and flush. Gaps and air pockets lose energy focus and cause uneven results.
7
Systematic delivery
Deliver shots along the pre-mapped grid lines, 5 mm spacing. Work methodically — do not jump or skip zones. Never deliver two consecutive pulses over the same coordinate.
8
Pain management
Expect a deep, hot, pricking sensation per shot. Reduce energy if intolerable, but do not drop below the therapeutic threshold without Medical Head approval.
9
Post-treatment
Cool the area. Lymphatic drainage. Log shots used per cartridge in ERP.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Never stack two pulses on the same coordinate — causes thermal focal necrosis
  • Loss of flush contact = wasted energy and uneven result
  • Sudden sharp radiating pain may indicate proximity to a nerve pathway — stop and reposition

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Cool the treated area
  • 5 minutes manual lymphatic drainage
  • Log cartridge shot count

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Drink 2.5–3 litres of water daily for 4 days
  • 20–30 minutes brisk walking within 4–6 hours
  • Expect tenderness, mild swelling and occasional tingling for up to 2 weeks

Avoid this

  • No hot bath, sauna or steam for 48 hours
  • No alcohol for 72 hours
  • No heavy refined carbohydrate for 72 hours

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Tenderness and mild swellingMinor (P4)Expected. Reassure. Document.
Thermal burnSerious (P2)Stop. Cold saline compress. Burn ointment. Call doctor + CM. Tag machine OOS. Log within 1 hour.
Prolonged numbness or nerve painSerious (P2)Doctor review urgently. Document. Do not retreat until cleared.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Face cartridge loaded for a body treatment
  • Fat caliper reading below 2.5 cm
  • Shot count not logged before starting
  • Treatment planned over the linea alba or umbilicus

Injection Lipolysis (Mesolipo)

Fat Dissolving Injection · Deoxycholic Acid / Phosphatidylcholine · Mesolipo
Session time20–40 minutesCourse3–5 sessionsIntervalEvery 4 weeksResults seen4–6 weeks, after swelling resolvesPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

A prescription injectable that chemically dissolves small, dense pockets of fat that do not respond to device-based treatments.

The mechanism

A lipolytic solution is injected in a grid pattern into the subcutaneous fat layer. It disrupts adipocyte membranes, and the released lipids are cleared by the lymphatic system and metabolised by the liver. Local inflammatory swelling for 3–7 days is expected and is part of the mechanism.

Equipment used

Injectable — 30G / 32G needles

Reference SOP

SOP-SLM-001 §2B · SOP-SLM-002 P2 · LIFE-SOP-INJ-001

2.0What it treats

  • Submental fat (double chin)
  • Bra fat
  • Lower abdomen
  • Small, dense, stubborn fat pockets not suited to cryo or cavitation

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+
  • Fat type. Small, localised, pinchable subcutaneous pocket
  • Blood thinners. None taken in the 72 hours before treatment
  • Skin. No infection, sores or open wounds in the area
  • Scarring. No keloid history in the treatment zone

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Aspirin, NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) or blood thinners in the last 72 hours
  • Active skin infection, sores or open wounds in the area
  • Keloid formation history in the treatment zone
  • Active cancer or malignancy
  • Severe hepatic or renal impairment
  • Uncontrolled diabetes
  • Known allergy to any component of the lipolytic solution

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Anticoagulant therapy — physician clearance
  • Bleeding disorders
  • Very thin overlying skin
  • Prior filler in the same area within 4 weeks
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Needle30G or 32G
Grid spacing1.0–1.5 cm; 1.0 cm for submental area
Injection depth4–6 mm, perpendicular (90°) into subcutaneous fat
Dose per point0.2 mL
Layer disciplineNever into muscle or dermis — dermal tracking causes blistering
Post-injection pressureFirm sterile gauze pressure for 2 minutes

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Pre-execution checklist
Confirm no aspirin, NSAIDs or blood thinners for 72 hours. No active infection or open wound. No keloid history. Not pregnant or breastfeeding. Signed injection-specific consent on file.
2
Skin sanitisation
Sanitise thoroughly with 70% isopropyl alcohol or chlorhexidine. Allow 30 seconds to dry.
3
Grid mapping
Apply a grid transfer tattoo at 1.0–1.5 cm spacing over the marked fat pocket. Do not mark or inject outside the boundary of pinchable subcutaneous fat.
4
Pinch and inject
Pinch the fat pouch away from underlying muscle. Insert perpendicular to 4–6 mm depth. Inject 0.2 mL per point. Withdraw swiftly to avoid superficial tracking.
5
Intra-procedure watch
Watch for immediate blanching (possible vascular compromise) or extreme sudden pain — either requires immediate cessation and physician evaluation.
6
Post-injection care
Firm sterile gauze pressure for 2 minutes. Cold compress for the burning sensation. Do NOT massage unless the specific product IFU mandates it.
7
Sharps disposal
All needles, syringes and vials directly into the yellow biohazard sharps container. Never into general waste.
8
Documentation
Log product, batch, total volume, number of points, area and client response in ERP and the Injectable Usage Register.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Immediate blanching = possible vascular compromise — stop and get physician evaluation
  • Extreme sudden pain = stop
  • When in doubt about post-injection massage: no massage, cold compress only

Before the client leaves the chair

  • 2 minutes firm pressure
  • Cold compress
  • Written swelling expectation brief — 3 to 7 days is normal

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Cold compress at home for the first 24 hours
  • Drink 2.5 litres of water daily
  • Expect swelling, tenderness and bruising for 3–7 days
  • Report hard nodules, spreading redness or skin colour change immediately

Avoid this

  • No massage of the area unless specifically instructed
  • No aspirin or NSAIDs for 48 hours unless prescribed
  • No alcohol for 48 hours
  • No hot bath, sauna or steam for 48 hours
  • Do not book the next session before 4 weeks

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Swelling, bruising, tendernessMinor (P4)Expected for 3–7 days. Cold compress. Reassure. Document.
Hard nodules or signs of necrosisSerious (P2)Immediate physician evaluation. Do NOT massage or manipulate. Physician decides on steroid injection or hyaluronidase. Log in ERP. Notify CM + COO.
Allergic reaction / anaphylaxisCritical (P1)Stop. First aid. Call 108 if severe. Doctor manages with epinephrine / antihistamine. Log within 1 hour. Notify Medical Head and COO.
Infection at injection siteSerious (P2)Doctor review. Antibiotic as prescribed. Photograph. Document. Incident SOP.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Client took aspirin, NSAIDs or blood thinners within 72 hours
  • Immediate blanching at any injection point
  • Injection outside the pinchable fat boundary
  • Needle or syringe reuse — absolute violation

EMSculpt / EMS Body Toning

RF-EMS · Electromagnetic Muscle Stimulation · EMS Belt · NMS
Session time30 minutes per zoneCourse4–6 sessionsIntervalEvery 2–3 daysResults seenProgressive; visible from session 3–4Performed byTrained therapist

1.0What this treatment is

High-intensity electromagnetic stimulation that produces supramaximal muscle contractions to build muscle definition and burn fat over the treated muscle group.

The mechanism

Focused electromagnetic energy induces involuntary muscle contractions far beyond what voluntary effort can achieve. The muscle responds with hypertrophy, and the metabolic demand drives localised lipolysis in the overlying fat.

Equipment used

EMSCULPT · EMS Belt · TENS/EMS unit

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 02 — EM Sculpt Treatment SOP · SOP-SLM-002 §1

2.0What it treats

  • Abdominal definition and core strengthening
  • Gluteal lifting
  • Arm and thigh toning
  • Post-partum core rehabilitation (with clearance)
  • Adjunct to fat reduction programmes

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+
  • Metal. No metal implants, plates or screws in or near the treatment area

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • IUD in place — do not treat the abdomen
  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Epilepsy or seizure disorder
  • Active cancer or malignancy
  • Recent surgery in the area within 6 months
  • Hernia in the treatment area
  • Severe cardiac or pulmonary disease
  • Active DVT or clotting disorder

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Uncontrolled hypertension
  • Uncontrolled diabetes
  • Recent abdominal surgery
  • Menstruation — abdominal treatment may be uncomfortable
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Session length30 minutes per zone
IntensityBuild progressively to client tolerance across the session
Applicator contactFull flat contact with the muscle belly — reposition if the contraction feels off-centre

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Screen contraindications
Screen every client before every session — metal, pacemaker, IUD, pregnancy, epilepsy, hernia, recent surgery.
2
Remove all metal
All jewellery, piercings, belts, phones and cards away from the applicator field.
3
Positioning
Position the client and secure the applicator flat over the target muscle belly.
4
Ramp intensity
Start low. Increase progressively over the first 5 minutes to the maximum comfortable level.
5
Monitor
Check comfort every 5 minutes. Contraction should be strong but not painful. Cramping = reduce.
6
Cool down
Machine cool-down / tapping phase at the end to reduce lactic soreness.
7
Documentation
Log zone, intensity reached, duration and response in ERP.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Sharp pain, cramping or pinching = reduce intensity immediately
  • Applicator shifting off the muscle belly = stop and reposition

  • Brief on expected muscle soreness for 24–48 hours
  • Encourage hydration and protein intake

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Drink 2 litres of water
  • Adequate protein intake to support muscle recovery
  • Expect soreness like after a hard workout for 24–48 hours

Avoid this

  • No intense workout of the same muscle group for 24 hours
  • Do not treat the same zone more often than every 2 days

GLP-1 Medical Weight Management

Semaglutide · Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) · Medical Weight Loss Injection
Session timeWeekly self-administered dose; monthly clinic reviewCourseContinuous programme with monthly titration reviewIntervalWeekly dose · monthly clinical review · Month 6 stop/goResults seenAssessed against a 5% total body weight loss benchmark at Month 6Performed byPrescribing doctor only. Non-prescribing therapists must not discuss or recommend GLP-1 independently.

1.0What this treatment is

A prescription-only pharmacological weight management programme using GLP-1 receptor agonists, delivered under strict clinical oversight with monthly monitoring and structured titration.

The mechanism

GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, increase satiety and reduce appetite signalling. Weight loss follows reduced caloric intake. The drug is an adjunct — nutrition, protein intake and resistance training are mandatory parts of the protocol, not optional extras.

Equipment used

Injectable — cold chain 2–8°C

Reference SOP

SOP-SLM-001 §6 · LIFE_GLP1_ERP_SOP · LIFE-SOP-INJ-001

2.0What it treats

  • BMI above 30
  • Age 27+ with at least one weight-related comorbidity: Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia or obstructive sleep apnoea

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Inclusion. BMI above 30 — OR — age 27+ with a weight-related comorbidity (T2D, HTN, dyslipidaemia, OSA)
  • Baseline labs. HbA1c, eGFR and LFTs ordered and reviewed before initiation
  • Baseline vitals. Weight, BMI, blood pressure, waist circumference recorded
  • Consent. Informed consent covering GI side effects, cost, perioperative fasting and long-term maintenance
  • Commitment. Willing to meet the protein and exercise protocol

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Personal or family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC) or MEN2
  • History of acute or chronic pancreatitis
  • Pregnancy, active breastfeeding, or planning pregnancy within 60 days
  • Known hypersensitivity to the drug or excipients
  • Type 1 diabetes (not an indication)

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Active gallbladder disease
  • Severe gastroparesis or significant GI motility disorder
  • Severe renal impairment — physician decision
  • History of eating disorder — psychological review first
  • Planned surgery or anaesthesia — see the aspiration risk protocol
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Titration principleEscalate ONLY if the current dose is well tolerated. Never accelerate the schedule.
Example — Tirzepatide2.5 mg weekly × 4 weeks → 5 mg → 7.5 mg → 10 mg → 12.5 mg → 15 mg (varies by individual response)
GI distress exceptionFreeze titration at the current dose for a further 2–4 weeks until symptoms resolve
Protein targetMinimum 60–80 g daily to prevent lean muscle wasting
Exercise targetMinimum 150 minutes moderate intensity weekly, including resistance training
StorageCold chain 2–8°C. Temperature log maintained daily.

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Baseline evaluation
Record weight, BMI, blood pressure, waist circumference. Order HbA1c, eGFR and LFTs.
2
Contraindication screen
Complete the full screening checklist. Any absolute contraindication stops the process.
3
Informed consent
Review GI side effects, out-of-pocket cost, perioperative fasting protocol and long-term maintenance expectations.
4
Initial dose & training
Dispense the lowest starter dose. Demonstrate subcutaneous self-injection technique in clinic.
5
Monthly titration review
Review at each monthly visit. Titrate up only if the current dose is well tolerated. Document the step in ERP.
6
Month 6 review
Assess against the 5% total body weight loss benchmark. GO = continue to maintenance at maximum tolerated dose with quarterly check-ins. STOP = taper over 2–4 weeks and pivot to alternative lifestyle or procedural therapy. Document the decision and rationale in ERP.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Never escalate the dose at a review where the client reports ongoing moderate GI symptoms
  • Any severe abdominal pain reported at review = hold dose, order lipase and amylase, refer to physician same day

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Confirm the client can demonstrate self-injection technique
  • Confirm next review date is booked
  • Confirm dietician consultation is scheduled

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Minimum 60–80 g protein daily to protect lean muscle
  • Small, frequent, nutrient-dense meals. Do not skip meals
  • Minimum 150 minutes moderate exercise weekly, including strength training
  • Store the pen at 2–8°C
  • Report severe abdominal pain or right upper quadrant pain immediately
  • Tell the clinic before any planned surgery or anaesthesia

Avoid this

  • Do not increase the dose yourself
  • Do not skip meals to accelerate loss
  • Avoid excess processed carbohydrate and sugar
  • Do not continue the drug into a planned pregnancy — inform the doctor first

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Nausea / early satietyMinor (P4)Halve portion sizes. Eat slowly, stop at the first fullness cue.
ConstipationMinor (P4)Increase hydration. High-fibre diet. OTC polyethylene glycol (macrogol) as appropriate.

Planned surgery or anaesthesiaSerious (P2)ASPIRATION RISK. Clear fluids only for 24 hours pre-procedure, or hold the drug for 1 week pre-operatively.
Injection site reactionMinor (P4)Rotate sites. Cold compress. Document.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Any family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2 disclosed at any point
  • Any history of pancreatitis
  • Client is pregnant, breastfeeding or planning pregnancy within 60 days
  • Non-prescribing staff discussing or recommending GLP-1 to a client
  • Dose escalated while the client still has moderate GI symptoms

Lymphatic Drainage & Whole Body Therapy

G5 / G10 Drainage · WBT with oil · Manual Lymphatic Drainage · FDS wrap
Session time20–45 minutesCourseAs prescribed alongside the contouring courseIntervalSame day as, or 24 hours after, cavitation / cryo / HIFUResults seenSupports and accelerates the primary treatment resultPerformed byTrained therapist

1.0What this treatment is

Mechanical and manual drainage that moves disrupted fat and interstitial fluid toward the lymph node clusters so the body can clear it.

The mechanism

Non-surgical fat reduction relies entirely on the lymphatic system to carry away disrupted adipocytes. Mechanical percussion, vibration and directed manual strokes accelerate that transport. Without it, mobilised lipids can be reabsorbed.

Equipment used

G5 Massager · G10 Massager · V1 Heat Blanket · V2 Vibration · Vibrator/Massager

Reference SOP

SOP-SLM-001 §3 · SOP-SLM-002 §6

2.0What it treats

  • Mandatory support after cavitation, cryolipolysis and HIFU
  • Fluid retention and puffiness
  • Post-treatment soreness
  • Inch-loss maintenance

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • General. Adults with intact skin over the treatment area
  • Post-treatment. Any client who has completed a fat-disruption treatment

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Active DVT or clotting disorder
  • Active infection or fever
  • Active cancer without oncologist clearance
  • Open wounds, ulcers or acute inflammation in the area
  • Pregnancy — abdominal work
  • Severe varicose veins in the area

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Recent surgery in the area
  • Very fragile or thin skin
  • Severe osteoporosis — reduce percussion intensity
  • Uncontrolled hypertension
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Stroke directionAlways toward the nearest lymph node cluster — groin for lower body, axilla for upper abdomen and torso
Manual drainage5 minutes minimum post-cavitation, cryo and HIFU
FDS application45 minutes post-session where prescribed
PercussionLight to moderate; never over bone, spine or kidney area

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Post-care cleansing
Remove all treatment gels. Apply the soothing post-treatment cream appropriate to the preceding modality.
2
Manual lymphatic drainage
5 minutes of upward strokes toward the nearest node cluster — groin for lower body, axilla for upper abdomen and torso.
3
Mechanical drainage
G5 / G10 percussion or vibration over the treated area. Avoid spine, kidney area and bony prominences.
4

1.0What this treatment is

A two-pass laser facial that uses a layer of medical-grade liquid carbon as a target for the laser, deep-cleaning pores and resurfacing the skin with zero downtime.

The mechanism

Liquid carbon penetrates the pores and binds dead skin, sebum and debris. The 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser is fired at low fluence; the carbon absorbs the energy and vaporises instantly, carrying the debris with it. The thermal effect also warms the dermis, stimulating collagen and tightening pores.

Session time20–40 minutesCourse3–15 sessions by indicationInterval2–6 weeks by indicationResults seenProgressive over the course; melasma requires strict sun disciplinePerformed byDoctor (MD / Diploma Dermatology). Doctor must be present.

1.0What this treatment is

Ultra-short, high-energy laser pulses that shatter unwanted pigment into microscopic fragments the body then clears, used for pigmentation, melasma, sun spots and overall skin brightening.

The mechanism

The Q-switched mechanism stores energy and releases it in nanosecond bursts. Melanin granules absorb the energy and fracture without heating surrounding tissue. 1064 nm reaches deep dermal pigment and vascular lesions; 532 nm targets superficial pigment and red/orange pigment. The fragments are cleared by the lymphatic and immune system over weeks.

Q-Switch Tattoo Removal

Laser Tattoo Removal
Session time15–45 minutes by tattoo sizeCourse6–15 (black ink) · 8–20 (colour ink)IntervalMinimum 6–8 weeks — required for immune clearanceResults seenProgressive fading; complete clearance is not guaranteedPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

Laser fragmentation of tattoo ink so the body's immune system can gradually clear it, delivered over a course of widely spaced sessions.

The mechanism

Nanosecond pulses shatter ink particles into fragments small enough for macrophages to carry away through the lymphatic system. Clearance happens between sessions, not during them — which is why the 6–8 week interval is non-negotiable.

Equipment used

Q-Switch Nd:YAG (1064 nm / 532 nm) · Pico Laser

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-CL-QS-001 Part B

2.0What it treats

  • Black and dark ink tattoos (1064 nm)
  • Coloured tattoos — red, orange, yellow (532 nm)
  • Partial fading before a cover-up
  • Amateur or traumatic tattoos

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+ with photo ID
  • Skin. Intact over the tattoo, no infection or sunburn
  • Expectations. Realistic — complete clearance is not guaranteed; some inks never fully clear
  • Consent. Written consent for each individual tattoo

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Active infection or open wound over the tattoo
  • Sunburned or recently tanned skin over the area
  • Isotretinoin within the last 6 months
  • Active cancer or on chemotherapy
  • Photosensitivity disorder or photosensitising medication
  • Keloid formation over the tattoo
  • Under 18 years

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Fitzpatrick V–VI — high PIH risk, 1064 nm and low fluence only
  • Unknown ink composition — risk of paradoxical darkening; test spot mandatory
  • Cosmetic / permanent makeup ink — high paradoxical darkening risk, dermatologist decision
  • Keloid history elsewhere
  • Diabetes — slower healing
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

1.0What this treatment is

Controlled application of an exfoliating acid to trigger the skin's healing cascade at a chosen depth — brightening, resurfacing, treating pigmentation and acne.

The mechanism

The acid causes a controlled injury to a predetermined depth. The skin responds with desquamation of damaged cells, accelerated cellular turnover and collagen remodelling. Depth is controlled by acid type, concentration, pH, number of layers, contact time, skin prep and prior retinoid use.

Equipment used

No machine — topical acid application

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-PEEL-001

2.0What it treats

  • Dull skin and uneven texture
  • Active acne and oily skin
  • Hyperpigmentation, melasma and PIH
  • Superficial acne scars
  • Fine lines and photodamage
  • Body areas: back acne, elbow and knee darkening, underarm pigmentation, rough heels

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Verify client
Confirm client ID, session number, peel type and treatment area in ERP and file.
2
Consent check
Signed consent in file. First session: confirm peel selection and that skin prep was completed.
3
Skin assessment
Examine under good lighting. Any red flag — STOP and consult the dermatologist.
4
Double cleanse
Twice with a gentle non-exfoliating cleanser. Remove all residue. Pat completely dry.
5
Degrease
Acetone, pre-peel solution or alcohol wipe to remove all surface oil. Critical — oil blocks penetration and creates uneven results.
6
Barrier protection
Gauze under the eyes; petroleum jelly barrier around eyes, nostrils and lips.
7
Peel application
Fan brush, gauze or cotton applicator in even strokes. Forehead → cheeks → nose → chin. Avoid eyes, nostrils, lips. Work quickly and methodically.
8
Layer control
Single layer for sensitive or darker skin. Second layer only on thicker or less sensitive areas and only if prescribed. Never multiple layers on the same area without dermatologist supervision.
9
Monitor endpoints
Watch erythema, frosting and client sensation. Stop at the correct endpoint for the peel type — see the frosting guide.
10
Time keeping
Timer from first application. Contact time per peel guide. Never exceed the maximum. Remove immediately on burning pain, blistering or distress.
11
Neutralise
AHA (Glycolic, Lactic, Mandelic, Pyruvic): neutraliser until fizzing stops. TCA: self-neutralising — do NOT apply water or neutraliser. Cosmelan / Yellow: removed at home per protocol.
12
Rinse
Cool water (not cold). Remove all residue. Pat gently dry.
13
Calm & cool
Cool compress 5 minutes, then Centella, aloe vera or the prescribed post-peel lotion.
14
Barrier repair
Light barrier cream or prescribed post-peel moisturiser. No heavy creams, actives or fragranced products.
15
SPF application
SPF 50+ as the final step before the client leaves. Mandatory.
16
Client handover
Verbal plus written instructions: timeline, what to expect, what to avoid, warning signs. Cosmelan / Yellow: give a written wash-off time.
17
ERP documentation
Peel, concentration, layers, contact time, endpoint observed, skin response, products applied.
18
Room care
Dispose of peel materials safely. Ventilate (especially Pyruvic). Store acids sealed and secure.

  • Burning pain, blistering or client distress — remove immediately
  • TCA: never apply water or neutraliser
  • Phenol: apply only one facial segment per 15 minutes to limit systemic absorption; cardiac monitoring required

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Cool compress 5–10 minutes — never ice directly on skin
  • Calming serum (Centella / aloe / prescribed)
  • Light barrier moisturiser
  • SPF 50+ — mandatory

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Use only the prescribed post-peel cream for the first 5 days
  • SPF 50+ every morning without fail
  • Let the skin shed naturally
  • Contact the clinic immediately for blistering, spreading redness, unusual pain or a herpes outbreak

Avoid this

  • DO NOT pick, peel or pull shedding skin — this causes PIH and scarring
  • No sun exposure for a minimum of 2 weeks
  • No active ingredients for a minimum of 5 days: retinol, AHA, BHA, Vitamin C, niacinamide, exfoliants

  • No waxing, threading or hair removal in the area for 2 weeks
  • No swimming or sea water for 1 week
  • No self-tanning or tanning beds for 4 weeks
  • No laser, IPL or energy device for a minimum of 4 weeks

1.0What this treatment is

A professional depigmentation system that suppresses melanin production at the enzyme level, used for stubborn melasma and hormonal hyperpigmentation — including on darker skin types.

The mechanism

A combination of azelaic, kojic, phytic and ascorbic acids with retinol inhibits tyrosinase, the enzyme that produces melanin. The clinic mask starts the process; the Cosmelan 2 home cream sustains the suppression. Without the home phase, results are incomplete and pigmentation returns.

MNRF — Microneedling Radiofrequency

Fractional RF · Micro Needle RF · D-MNRF · Morpheus-type RF microneedling
Session time45–75 minutes including numbingCourse3–6 sessionsInterval4–6 weeksResults seenProgressive; peak collagen result at 3 months after the final sessionPerformed byDoctor performs; doctor assistant supports

1.0What this treatment is

Insulated micro-needles deliver radiofrequency energy directly into the dermis, remodelling acne scars, tightening skin and refining pores with minimal surface damage.

The mechanism

The needles bypass the epidermis and deposit RF energy at a controlled dermal depth. The thermal injury zones trigger a wound-healing cascade — new collagen and elastin — while the surface heals within days. Because the epidermis is largely spared, PIH risk is lower than with ablative resurfacing, which makes it well suited to Indian skin.

Equipment used

MNRF Machine · Fractional RF platform

Reference SOP

1.0What this treatment is

Focused ultrasound delivered at three fixed depths to lift and tighten the face and neck, including the SMAS layer that a surgical facelift targets — without any incision.

The mechanism

Energy is focused at 1.5 mm (superficial dermis), 3.0 mm (deep dermis) and 4.5 mm (SMAS / fascial layer), creating discrete coagulation points at depth while the skin surface stays intact. The tissue contracts immediately and then remodels with new collagen over the following 8–12 weeks.

The client's own concentrated platelets, drawn from their blood and reintroduced into the skin, to accelerate repair, improve texture and stimulate collagen.

The mechanism

Blood is drawn and spun in a centrifuge to separate platelet-rich plasma. Platelets carry growth factors — PDGF, TGF-β, VEGF — that drive fibroblast activity, angiogenesis and collagen synthesis. The PRP is delivered by injection or through microneedling channels.

Equipment used

Centrifuge · vacutainer tubes · Derma Pen for delivery

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 20 (PRP Consent) · FORM 21 (PRP Treatment & Record Sheet)

2.0What it treats

  • Dull, tired skin and loss of glow
  • Fine lines and early ageing
  • Acne scars (with microneedling)
  • Under-eye hollowing and dark circles
  • Post-procedure healing acceleration

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+
  • Blood. Adequate platelet count; no bleeding disorder
  • Skin. No active infection in the treatment field
  • Consent. Signed PRP consent covering the blood draw

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Platelet disorders, thrombocytopenia or bleeding disorder
  • Active anticoagulation therapy
  • Active infection at the treatment or draw site
  • Sepsis or systemic infection
  • Active cancer, especially haematological malignancy
  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Severe anaemia
  • Chronic liver disease
  • Active herpes in the treatment field

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Recent NSAID use — reduces platelet function; advise a 7-day gap
  • Smoking — reduces efficacy
  • Poorly controlled diabetes
  • Autoimmune connective tissue disease
  • Isotretinoin within 6 months
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

IV Skin Glow & Antioxidant Drips

Glutathione IV · Vitamin C Infusion · Gluta Glow · IV Anti-Ageing Drip
Session time30–60 minutes per infusionCourse6–10 sessionsIntervalWeekly or fortnightlyResults seenProgressive brightening over the course; maintenance requiredPerformed byDoctor only. Doctor must remain on site for the whole infusion.

1.0What this treatment is

An intravenous infusion of antioxidants — most commonly glutathione with Vitamin C — used for skin brightening, antioxidant support and general wellness.

The mechanism

Glutathione is the body's principal intracellular antioxidant and inhibits tyrosinase, shifting melanin production toward lighter pheomelanin. Vitamin C regenerates glutathione and supports collagen synthesis. IV delivery bypasses gut absorption limits.

Equipment used

IV infusion set · cold chain storage

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-INJ-001 · Clinical Forms FORM 23 (Glutathione Consent)

2.0What it treats

  • Overall skin brightening and evenness
  • Antioxidant and wellness support
  • Adjunct to a pigmentation programme
  • Post-sun-damage support

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+
  • Pre-drip assessment. Doctor pre-drip assessment completed and documented
  • Veins. Adequate venous access
  • Consent. Signed glutathione / IV consent with the off-label position explained

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Known allergy to glutathione, Vitamin C or any infusion component
  • G6PD deficiency (high-dose Vitamin C — haemolysis risk)
  • Renal impairment or history of oxalate kidney stones (high-dose Vitamin C)
  • Active asthma with sulphite sensitivity
  • Active cancer without oncologist clearance
  • Severe cardiac or renal failure — fluid load

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Anaemia

  • Diabetes — glucose interaction with high-dose Vitamin C
  • Poor venous access
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.
