Botulinum Toxin (Botox)

Botox · Anti-wrinkle Injection · Botulinum Toxin Type A
Session time20–30 minutesCourseSingle session; repeat at 3–4 monthsIntervalMinimum 3 months between treatments to the same areaResults seenOnset 3–7 days, peak at 14 days, lasts 3–4 monthsPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

A prescription injectable that temporarily relaxes specific facial muscles to soften dynamic wrinkles, slim the jaw, or reduce sweating.

The mechanism

Botulinum toxin type A blocks acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, temporarily reducing muscle contraction. The overlying skin stops creasing and existing lines soften. The effect wears off as new nerve terminals form over 3–4 months.

Equipment used

Injectable — cold chain 2–8°C

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 13 (Botox Pictorial Record Sheet) · LIFE-SOP-INJ-001

2.0What it treats

  • Glabellar frown lines
  • Forehead lines
  • Crow's feet
  • Bunny lines and gummy smile
  • Masseter reduction / jaw slimming
  • Platysmal neck bands
  • Axillary hyperhidrosis (excess sweating)

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+; typically 25+ for dynamic lines
  • Health. No neuromuscular disorder
  • Expectations. Softening of dynamic lines; static deep lines need combination treatment
  • Timing. Not within 2 weeks of a major event — allow settling time

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Neuromuscular disorders: myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton syndrome, ALS
  • Known hypersensitivity to botulinum toxin or albumin
  • Active infection at the injection site
  • Aminoglycoside antibiotics in current use — potentiates the toxin
  • Body dysmorphic presentation or unrealistic fixed expectations

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Bleeding disorder or anticoagulation — bruising risk
  • Previous unsatisfactory result or ptosis with toxin
  • Asymmetry present before treatment — must be photographed and discussed
  • Recent facial surgery
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Stay upright for 4 hours
  • Animate the treated muscles gently for the first hour
  • Expect onset at 3–7 days and full effect at 14 days
  • Attend the 2-week review
  • Report drooping of the eyelid or brow immediately

Avoid this

  • No facial, sauna, steam or hot yoga for 24 hours

  • No alcohol for 24 hours
  • Do not judge the result before 14 days

Session time30–60 minutesCourseSingle session; top-up per product longevityInterval6–18 months depending on product and areaResults seenImmediate, settling over 2 weeksPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

Injectable hyaluronic acid gel used to restore volume, define contours and smooth static lines.

The mechanism

Cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel is placed in a specific tissue plane to add volume and structure. It also draws water, adding hydration. It is gradually broken down by the body over 6–18 months, and can be dissolved with hyaluronidase if needed.

Equipment used

Injectable — needle and cannula technique

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 18 (Dermal Fillers Consent) · FORM 17 (Hyaluronidase Consent)

2.0What it treats

  • Cheek and mid-face volume loss

  • Tear trough hollowing
  • Hand rejuvenation
  • Skin quality boosters (Profhilo, Skinvive, Volite, Viscoderm)

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Active autoimmune disease flare

  • Body dysmorphic presentation

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Recent dental work — space by 2 weeks (bacteraemia risk)
  • Herpes history around the lips — antiviral prophylaxis required for lip filler
  • Prior filler of unknown type in the area
  • Planned surgery or vaccination within 2 weeks
  • History of keloid
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Thread Lift

PDO Threads · COG Threads · Mono Threads · Non-Surgical Lift
Session time45–90 minutesCourseSingle session; repeat at 12–18 monthsInterval12–18 monthsResults seenImmediate lift; collagen result builds over 3 monthsPerformed byDoctor only, with thread-specific training

1.0What this treatment is

Absorbable barbed or smooth sutures placed under the skin to lift sagging tissue and stimulate collagen along the thread path.

The mechanism

COG (barbed) threads anchor into the tissue and mechanically reposition it upward. Mono (smooth) threads do not lift but stimulate collagen along their length. Both are made of polydioxanone, which dissolves over 6–8 months while the collagen it induced persists.

Equipment used

Injectable — cannula and needle threads

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 15 (Thread Lift Consent)

2.0What it treats

  • Mid-face and jowl sagging
  • Jawline definition
  • Brow lift
  • Neck laxity
  • Collagen stimulation (mono threads)

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. Typically 35–60
  • Laxity. Mild to moderate — severe sagging needs surgery, not threads
  • Skin. Adequate skin thickness; very thin skin risks visible threads
  • Expectations. A lift of a few millimetres, not a facelift result

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Active skin infection or inflammation in the field
  • Known allergy to polydioxanone
  • Autoimmune disease flare
  • Bleeding disorder or active anticoagulation
  • Active cancer or on chemotherapy
  • Severe skin laxity where the result would be inadequate — refer for surgical opinion

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Very thin skin — thread visibility risk
  • Previous thread lift with residual material
  • Keloid tendency
  • Recent filler in the same plane
  • Smoking — impairs healing
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Thread typeCOG for lifting; mono for collagen stimulation
Entry pointsMarked and photographed before insertion
Danger zonesFacial nerve branches, parotid duct, major vessels — anatomical knowledge is mandatory
SterilityFull sterile field, sterile drape, sterile gloves. This is a minor surgical procedure
AntibioticPer doctor protocol

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Consult and assess
Assess laxity and skin thickness. Photograph from standard angles including animation. Discuss realistic lift.
2
Consent
Signed FORM 15 covering visible threads, extrusion, dimpling, asymmetry, infection and limited longevity.
3
Mark the plan
Mark entry points and vectors with the client upright. Photograph the marked plan.
4
Sterile preparation
Full antisepsis, sterile drape, sterile gloves and instruments.
5
Local anaesthesia
Entry point anaesthesia and along the vector as required.
6
Thread placement
Insert in the correct plane along the marked vector. Engage and lift. Check symmetry with the client sitting up.
7
Trim and close
Trim thread ends below the skin surface. Confirm no thread is palpable at the surface.
8
Immediate post
Cold compress. Antibiotic cover per protocol. Detailed movement restrictions given in writing.
9
Documentation
Thread type, number, batch, vectors, entry points in ERP. Photograph. Book a 1-week and 1-month review.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Sharp radiating pain or facial twitch = stop, withdraw and reposition — possible nerve proximity
  • Thread visible or palpable at the surface = reposition before finishing
  • Asymmetry must be corrected at the chair, not at review

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Cold compress
  • Antibiotic cover per protocol
  • Written movement restrictions
  • 1-week and 1-month reviews booked

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Sleep on your back with the head elevated for 1 week
  • Eat soft food for 3–5 days
  • Expect swelling, bruising and a tight pulling sensation for 1–2 weeks
  • Report thread extrusion, spreading redness, pus or fever immediately

Avoid this

  • No wide mouth opening, chewing gum or big facial expressions for 2 weeks
  • No facial massage or facials for 4 weeks
  • No dental work for 2 weeks
  • No sleeping on your side or face for 1 week
  • No gym or sauna for 2 weeks

  • Non-sterile technique at any point
  • Thread palpable at the skin surface at the end of the procedure
  • Facial twitching during insertion
  • Severe laxity being treated with threads instead of a surgical referral

Mole, Wart, Skin Tag & Keloid Management

Naevus Removal · Wart Cautery · Skin Tag Removal · Kenacort for Keloid
Session time15–30 minutesCourse1–3 sessions depending on lesionInterval3–4 weeks where repeat treatment is neededResults seenImmediate removal; healing over 7–14 daysPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

Removal or treatment of benign skin lesions — moles, warts, skin tags, milia — and intralesional steroid treatment for keloid and hypertrophic scars.

The mechanism

Radiofrequency cautery or cryotherapy destroys the lesion tissue at a controlled depth, leaving a small wound that heals by secondary intention. Keloids are treated with intralesional triamcinolone, which flattens the scar by suppressing fibroblast activity.

Equipment used

Radiofrequency cautery · WARTS QUARTERY unit · CO2 cylinder (cryotherapy)

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 19 (Mole / Naevus Removal Consent) · FORM 22 (Skin Biopsy Consent)

2.0What it treats

  • Benign moles and naevi (cosmetic removal)
  • Viral warts and verrucae
  • Skin tags (acrochordons)
  • Milia and syringoma
  • Keloid and hypertrophic scars (intralesional steroid)
  • Seborrhoeic keratoses

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Assessment. Every pigmented lesion must be assessed by the doctor for malignancy features BEFORE any removal
  • Age. 18+; paediatric cases by specific paediatric consent
  • Consent. Signed removal consent; biopsy consent where histology is planned

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • ANY lesion with suspicious features — asymmetry, irregular border, colour variation, diameter over 6 mm, recent change, bleeding or itching. These must be referred for dermatology assessment and histopathology, NEVER cosmetically destroyed
  • Active infection at the site
  • Pregnancy — elective removal deferred
  • Bleeding disorder or active anticoagulation without clearance
  • Uncontrolled diabetes — poor healing
  • Keloid tendency for elective cosmetic removal

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Keloid-prone site: chest, shoulders, upper back, jawline
  • Fitzpatrick V–VI — higher PIH and keloid risk; counsel carefully
  • Immunosuppression — recurrent warts
  • Multiple lesions — stage across sessions
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Malignancy screenMandatory doctor assessment of every pigmented lesion before removal. If in doubt — biopsy, do not destroy
HistologyAny lesion sent for histology must be recorded with the lab, date and report tracked to closure
DepthControlled, superficial. Over-treatment causes scarring
KenacortIntralesional triamcinolone, dose per lesion size, repeat at 3–4 week intervals

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Doctor assessment
Full lesion assessment including dermoscopy where available. Screen for malignancy features. Photograph with a scale marker.
2
Decision
Suspicious features = refer / biopsy. Never cosmetically destroy a lesion you have not confidently assessed as benign.
3
Consent
Signed consent covering scarring, pigmentation change, recurrence and — for pigmented lesions — the loss of histology if destroyed.
4
Antisepsis and anaesthesia
Antiseptic prep. Local anaesthetic infiltration.
5
Removal
RF cautery or cryotherapy to a controlled superficial depth. Do not over-treat.
6
Histology if indicated
Where excision is done, place the specimen in formalin, label with client ID and site, and log the lab dispatch.
7
Dressing
Antibiotic ointment and dressing. Written wound care.
8
Documentation
Lesion type, site, method, specimen sent (Y/N), lab reference in ERP. Book the review and — if histology was sent — a report review appointment.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Unexpected bleeding, deep pigment or an irregular base = stop and reassess for malignancy
  • Do not chase depth to guarantee no recurrence — recurrence is preferable to a scar

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Antibiotic ointment and dressing
  • Written wound care
  • Review booked; histology report review booked where applicable

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Keep the area clean and dry for 48 hours
  • Apply the prescribed ointment as directed
  • Allow the scab to fall off naturally
  • SPF 50+ on the healed area for 3 months to prevent dark marks
  • Report spreading redness, pus, fever or heavy bleeding immediately
  • Attend the histology report appointment if a specimen was sent

Avoid this

  • Do not pick or remove the scab
  • No swimming or sauna until healed
  • No sun exposure on the site during healing
  • Do not apply any home remedy to the wound

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Scab and mild rednessMinor (P4)Normal healing. Reassure. Document.
Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentationModerate (P3)Common in Indian skin. Strict SPF. Dermatologist review. Document and counsel.
Hypertrophic or keloid scarSerious (P2)Dermatologist review. Intralesional steroid or silicone. Document.
InfectionSerious (P2)Doctor review. Antibiotic. Photograph. Incident SOP.
RecurrenceMinor (P4)Reassess. Repeat treatment or refer. Document.
Missed malignancyCritical (P1)Never destroy an unassessed pigmented lesion. If suspicion arises after removal, urgent dermatology and oncology referral. Escalate to Medical Head and COO immediately.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Any pigmented lesion with ABCDE features being cosmetically destroyed
  • Client reports the mole has recently changed, bled or itched
  • Removal proceeding without doctor assessment
  • Specimen sent to lab with no tracking record

Permanent Makeup (PMU) & Microblading

Microblading Eyebrows · Lip Micropigmentation · Cosmetic Tattooing
Session time90–150 minutesCourse1 session + 1 mandatory touch-up at 4–6 weeksIntervalTouch-up at 4–6 weeks; colour boost at 12–18 monthsResults seenSettles at 4 weeks; final colour after the touch-upPerformed byCertified PMU artist. Doctor available on site.
Awaiting medical sign-offThis treatment has no dedicated written LIFE SOP yet. What follows is the standard clinical method for the modality, assembled to the same structure as our other protocols. It must be reviewed and signed by the Medical Head before it is circulated as LIFE policy.

1.0What this treatment is

Cosmetic pigment implanted into the upper dermis to shape eyebrows, define lips or enhance the lash line, lasting 12–24 months.

The mechanism

Pigment is deposited into the superficial dermis with a blade or machine needle. Because it sits shallower than a body tattoo, the body gradually breaks it down, so the result fades over 12–24 months rather than being permanent in the tattoo sense.

Equipment used

PMU device · microblading hand tool · single-use sterile cartridges and blades

Reference SOP

[TO CONFIRM] — dedicated LIFE PMU SOP required. Below is the standard safe-practice framework pending Medical Head sign-off

2.0What it treats

  • Sparse, thin or asymmetric eyebrows
  • Alopecia and post-chemotherapy brow loss
  • Lip colour correction and definition
  • Lip pigmentation camouflage
  • Scar camouflage in the brow area

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+ with photo ID
  • Skin. Intact, no active infection, acne or dermatitis in the area
  • Health. No bleeding disorder; not on active anticoagulation
  • Consent. Signed consent, patch test done, before photographs taken

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Active skin infection, acne or dermatitis in the area
  • Active herpes simplex — for lip PMU, antiviral prophylaxis is mandatory and active outbreak is an absolute bar
  • Keloid tendency
  • Bleeding disorder or active anticoagulation
  • Isotretinoin within the last 6 months
  • Active cancer or on chemotherapy / radiotherapy
  • Uncontrolled diabetes
  • Known allergy to pigment components — patch test mandatory
  • Under 18 years

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Very oily skin — pigment retention is poorer, counsel expectations
  • Previous PMU with unknown pigment — colour correction is complex
  • Recent botox or filler in the area — space by 2 weeks
  • Keloid-prone skin
  • Immunosuppression
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
DepthSuperficial dermis only. Too deep = blue-grey migration and permanence
Blades and cartridgesSingle use, sterile, opened in front of the client. Never reused
PigmentBatch and expiry recorded. Patch test 48 hours before first session
AntiviralMandatory prophylaxis for lip PMU with any herpes history
Touch-upAt 4–6 weeks — the result is not complete without it

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Consult and patch test
Discuss shape, colour and expectations. Patch test 48 hours before. Photograph.
2
Consent
Signed consent covering fading, colour shift, need for touch-up, infection and the semi-permanent nature.
3
Antiviral cover
For lip PMU with any herpes history — antiviral started per doctor prescription before the session.
4
Design and approve
Draw the shape with the client sitting upright. Client approves in the mirror and signs off on the design before any pigment.
5
Numbing
Topical anaesthetic. Remove completely before starting.
6
Sterile setup
Open new sterile blade or cartridge in front of the client. Gloves. Barrier-wrapped equipment.
7
Implantation
Work to the superficial dermal depth only. Consistent pressure and angle. Check symmetry repeatedly with the client upright.
8
Aftercare handover
Apply the prescribed ointment. Give detailed written aftercare and the wash instruction.
9
Disposal and documentation
Blade/cartridge to sharps. Log pigment brand, colour, batch, expiry and technique in ERP. Book the 4–6 week touch-up.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Excessive bleeding = working too deep, lift the angle
  • Client reporting sharp pain despite numbing = reassess depth
  • Never proceed if the design has not been approved by the client in the mirror

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Prescribed ointment
  • Detailed written aftercare
  • Touch-up appointment booked at 4–6 weeks

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Blot the area gently as instructed for the first day
  • Apply the prescribed ointment thinly as directed
  • Expect the colour to look dark for 5–7 days, then flake and lighten by 40% before settling
  • Attend the touch-up at 4–6 weeks
  • Report spreading redness, pus, swelling or fever immediately

Avoid this

  • Do not pick or scratch the flaking pigment — it pulls the pigment out and causes patches
  • No makeup on the area for 7 days
  • No swimming, sauna, steam or heavy sweating for 14 days
  • No sun exposure or tanning for 4 weeks
  • No retinol, AHA, BHA or exfoliants on or near the area for 4 weeks

Patchy healing / pigment lossMinor (P4)Common — this is what the touch-up corrects. Reassure. Document.

  • Lip PMU on a client with herpes history and no antiviral cover
  • Client did not approve the drawn design before pigment was implanted
  • Excessive bleeding indicating depth error

Laser Hair Removal

Laser Hair Removal (Diode)

LHR · Laser Hair Reduction · Diode Laser
Session time10–90 minutes depending on areaCourse6–8 sessions for optimum resultInterval4–12 weeks depending on body areaResults seenProgressive reduction; permanent reduction, not guaranteed 100% removalPerformed byTrained and certified LHR therapist. Doctor must be on site — mandatory.

1.0What this treatment is

Targeted laser energy that disables hair follicles during their active growth phase, permanently reducing unwanted hair over a course of sessions.

The mechanism

Selective photothermolysis. The 808 nm diode wavelength is absorbed by melanin in the hair shaft and follicle. The heat generated destroys the follicle's ability to produce new hair while contact cooling protects the epidermis. Only hairs in the active (anagen) phase respond, which is why multiple sessions spaced across the growth cycle are required.

Equipment used

Diode Laser (808 nm core; 755/940 nm multi-wavelength models)

Reference SOP

LIFE-SOP-LHR-001 · Clinical Forms FORM 07, 08, 09

2.0What it treats

  • Face — upper lip, chin, sideburns, beard line, full face
  • Underarms
  • Arms — half and full
  • Legs — half and full
  • Back and chest
  • Bikini and Brazilian
  • Full body
  • Male grooming — beard shaping, back and chest

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+; under 18 only with guardian consent and doctor approval
  • Skin type. Fitzpatrick I–VI with adjusted parameters. V–VI require dermatologist review before treatment
  • Hair. Dark, pigmented hair responds best. Grey, white and very fine blonde hair does not respond
  • Preparation. Area shaved 12–24 hours before — never waxed, threaded or plucked
  • Skin condition. No tan (natural or artificial) in the last 4 weeks
  • Expectations. Permanent reduction over 6–8 sessions. 100% removal is not guaranteed

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Active skin infection, open wounds or active herpes in the treatment area
  • Pregnancy (any trimester)
  • Known photosensitivity disorder or light-triggered seizures
  • Active skin cancer or history of melanoma
  • Isotretinoin (Accutane) within the last 6 months
  • Tattoos or permanent makeup in the direct treatment area
  • Tanned skin — natural or artificial — in the last 4 weeks

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Fitzpatrick Type V or VI — dermatologist review mandatory
  • Anticoagulant, photosensitising or hormonal medications
  • History of keloid or hypertrophic scarring
  • Active autoimmune disorders — lupus, vitiligo, psoriasis in the area
  • Pacemaker or metal implants near the treatment area
  • History of gold therapy
  • Poorly controlled diabetes
  • PCOS — hormonal regrowth; counsel that maintenance sessions will be needed
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Patch test protocol

  • MANDATORY for: all NEW clients · all Fitzpatrick IV–VI · any client returning after a gap of more than 6 months
  • Select a 2 cm × 2 cm test area in the treatment zone
  • Apply the lowest appropriate fluence for the skin type
  • Observe for 10 minutes for immediate reaction
  • Client returns after 24–48 hours for review. Proceed only if no adverse reaction
  • Document the patch test result in ERP and in the physical treatment file

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Client verification
Confirm client name, ID, session number and treatment area against ERP and the treatment file.
2
Consent check
Confirm the signed consent form is in the file for this session.
3
Skin assessment
Re-examine the area. Check for active lesions, cuts, rash or tan. If found, do not proceed.
4
Area preparation
Cleanse with a gentle non-alcoholic cleanser. Pat dry thoroughly.
5
Shaving confirmation
Confirm the area was shaved 12–24 hours prior. If not, the therapist shaves — never wax or thread.
6
Apply cooling gel
Thin, even layer of ultrasound / cooling gel over the area.
7
Eye protection
Certified laser safety goggles on client and therapist before firing. Non-negotiable.
8
Machine settings
Set fluence, pulse width and frequency per the Fitzpatrick guide. Do NOT exceed recommended parameters.
9
Test pulse
Fire one test pulse on a small area. Wait 30 seconds. Observe the skin reaction before proceeding.
10
Treatment delivery
Sliding or stamping technique. Move methodically with 10–20% overlap. Ensure full coverage.
11
Client monitoring
Ask about pain and heat every 2–3 minutes on a 1–10 scale. Above 6 — reduce fluence immediately.
12
Cooling during
Cool compress or integrated cooling as required. Never leave the client unattended.
13
Gel removal
Remove gel with clean, soft gauze. Do NOT rub aggressively.
14
Post-treatment application
Soothing aloe vera gel or the prescribed post-LHR cream. No ice directly on skin.
15
Client instructions
Verbal and written post-treatment instructions before the client leaves.
16
ERP documentation
Update the session immediately — parameters used, skin response, observations.
17
Machine shutdown
Clean the handpiece with the recommended solution. Power down per manufacturer instructions.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Pain score above 6 out of 10 = reduce fluence immediately
  • Immediate greying, whitening or blistering of the skin = stop
  • Client reports a burning smell beyond the normal singed-hair smell = stop
  • Goggles dislodging = stop and replace before continuing

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Soothing aloe or prescribed cream
  • No ice directly on skin — wrap in cloth if cooling is needed
  • Monitor 15 minutes for adverse reaction
  • Document all observations in ERP before the client leaves

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Shave between sessions — shaving is permitted and encouraged
  • Avoid sun on the treated area for a minimum of 2 weeks; SPF 50+ daily
  • Expect mild redness and small bumps around the follicles for 24–48 hours — this is normal
  • Attend within 2 weeks of noticing new regrowth for the best result
  • Report blistering, significant pain or skin colour change immediately

Avoid this

  • Do NOT wax, thread, pluck or epilate between sessions — this removes the target
  • No hot showers, steam, sauna or swimming for 48 hours
  • No perfume, deodorant or harsh products on the area for 48 hours
  • No scratching or scrubbing the area
  • No sunbed or tanning during the course

EventSeverityImmediate action

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • No patch test on a new client or a Fitzpatrick IV–VI client
  • Client has a tan or recent sun exposure
  • Isotretinoin within 6 months disclosed
  • Tattoo or permanent makeup in the treatment field
  • Client waxed or threaded instead of shaving
  • Goggles not on both client and therapist
  • Doctor not on site

Hair PRP

Platelet Rich Plasma — Scalp · Booster PRP · Hair PRP Basic
Session time45–60 minutes including draw and spinCourse4–6 sessions in the initial courseInterval4 weeks; then maintenance every 3–6 monthsResults seenReduced shedding by 6–8 weeks; visible density change at 3–6 monthsPerformed byDoctor only

1.0What this treatment is

The client's own concentrated platelets injected into the scalp to reduce hair fall and stimulate weakened follicles into stronger growth.

The mechanism

Platelets release growth factors — PDGF, VEGF, IGF-1 — that increase blood supply to the dermal papilla, prolong the anagen (growth) phase and thicken miniaturised follicles. It strengthens existing hair; it cannot regrow follicles that are completely lost.

Equipment used

PRP Machine (centrifuge) · vacutainer tubes

Reference SOP

Clinical Forms FORM 20 (PRP Consent) · FORM 21 (PRP Record Sheet)

2.0What it treats

  • Androgenetic alopecia — male and female pattern
  • Telogen effluvium and diffuse thinning
  • Post-partum hair fall
  • Hair thinning after weight loss or illness
  • Adjunct after hair transplant to support graft survival

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. 18+
  • Follicles. Miniaturised but present follicles — PRP cannot revive a fully bald, shiny scalp
  • Blood. Adequate platelet count, no bleeding disorder
  • Expectations. Reduced fall first, density second. Maintenance is required indefinitely

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Platelet disorders, thrombocytopenia or bleeding disorder
  • Active anticoagulation therapy
  • Active scalp infection — folliculitis, fungal infection, open wounds
  • Sepsis or systemic infection
  • Active cancer, especially haematological malignancy
  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding
  • Severe anaemia
  • Chronic liver disease
  • Uncontrolled diabetes

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Recent NSAID use — reduces platelet function; advise a 7-day gap
  • Smoking — measurably reduces efficacy
  • Active seborrhoeic dermatitis — treat the scalp first
  • Untreated thyroid disorder or iron deficiency — treat the cause first or results will be poor
  • Isotretinoin within 6 months
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Draw volumePer kit protocol

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Consult and diagnose
Confirm the type of hair loss. Trichoscopy where available. Order thyroid, ferritin, Vitamin D and CBC where indicated — treating PRP without correcting a deficiency wastes the course.
2
Consent and photos
Signed FORM 20. Standardised scalp photographs — same parting, same lighting, same angles.
3
Blood draw
Aseptic draw into labelled vacutainer tubes. Label at the chair in front of the client.
4
Centrifuge
Spin per kit protocol. Confirm clean separation of the platelet layer.
5
Prepare the scalp
Part and clean the scalp with antiseptic. Numb if required.
6
Extract PRP
Draw off the platelet-rich layer aseptically.
7
Injection
Deliver in a 1 cm grid across the thinning zone at 4–6 mm depth. Small volume per point.
8
Post-treatment
Do not wash the scalp for 24 hours. No styling product. Give written aftercare.
9
Disposal and documentation
Sharps and tubes to biohazard. Complete FORM 21. Log volume, zones and response in ERP. Book the next session at 4 weeks.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Any doubt about tube identity = discard and redraw
  • Vasovagal reaction during the draw is common — lay flat, elevate legs
  • Bleeding points on the scalp are normal; persistent bleeding is not

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Written aftercare with the 24-hour no-wash rule
  • Next session booked
  • Photographs filed

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Expect scalp tenderness and mild swelling for 24–48 hours
  • Wash your hair normally after 24 hours with a mild shampoo
  • Take any prescribed supplements — PRP works best alongside correction of deficiency
  • Attend all sessions in the course; skipping breaks the cycle
  • Continue maintenance every 3–6 months to hold the result

Avoid this

  • Do not wash the scalp for 24 hours
  • No hair colour, chemical treatment or straightening for 72 hours
  • No swimming, sauna or steam for 48 hours
  • No NSAIDs for 48 hours after
  • No head massage with oil for 48 hours

HFT High Frequency Therapy · Scalp Peel · Anti-Dandruff Treatment · Anti-Hairfall Therapy · Mesotherapy Hair

1.0What this treatment is

A group of scalp-directed treatments — exfoliating peels, high-frequency therapy, low-level laser and nutrient mesotherapy — used to treat the scalp environment so hair can grow properly.

The mechanism

Scalp peels clear follicular build-up and flaking. High-frequency current is antimicrobial and increases local circulation. Low-level laser stimulates cellular metabolism in the follicle. Mesotherapy delivers vitamins, peptides and vasodilators directly to the dermal papilla. Most hair loss cases need the scalp treated before follicle-stimulating treatments will work.

Equipment used

High-frequency wand · E-Scope (Hair) · Laser Dome / laser photo therapy

[TO CONFIRM] — dedicated LIFE scalp therapy SOP required

  • Dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis

  • Diffuse hair fall

Hair Transplant (FUE)

Follicular Unit Extraction · HT · Hair Restoration Surgery
Session time6–10 hours depending on graft countCourseSingle procedure; occasionally a second session at 12 monthsIntervalMinimum 12 months before a second sessionResults seenShedding at 2–4 weeks, regrowth from 3–4 months, final result at 12–18 monthsPerformed byHair transplant surgeon with a trained HT team

1.0What this treatment is

A surgical procedure in which individual follicular units are extracted from the permanent donor zone at the back and sides of the scalp and implanted into thinning or bald areas.

The mechanism

Follicles in the occipital donor zone are genetically resistant to DHT, the hormone that miniaturises hair in pattern baldness. When transplanted, they retain that resistance and continue to grow in their new site for life. The transplanted hair sheds at 2–4 weeks — this is normal — and regrows from the retained follicle at 3–4 months.

Equipment used

FUE punch system · implanters · dedicated HT theatre

Reference SOP

LIFE HT document set — consultation form, surgery booking card, floor checklist, pre/post-operative SOPs, patient handout

2.0What it treats

  • Male pattern baldness — Norwood grades II–VI with an adequate donor
  • Female pattern hair loss with a stable donor zone
  • Frontal hairline restoration
  • Crown filling
  • Beard and moustache transplant
  • Eyebrow transplant
  • Scar camouflage — post-surgical or burn scars

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • Age. Usually 25+; younger clients risk chasing a progressing pattern
  • Donor. Adequate donor density in the permanent zone — assessed and documented by the surgeon
  • Stability. Hair loss pattern reasonably stable, or being medically stabilised
  • Health. Fit for a long day procedure under local anaesthesia; controlled BP and blood sugar
  • Expectations. Understands coverage is redistribution, not new hair; realistic density targets
  • Bloods. Pre-operative screen completed and reviewed

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Insufficient donor density for meaningful coverage
  • Active scalp infection or inflammatory scalp disease
  • Uncontrolled diabetes or uncontrolled hypertension
  • Bleeding disorder or active anticoagulation not cleared by a physician
  • Active cancer or on chemotherapy
  • Unstable cardiac disease
  • Keloid tendency on the scalp
  • Body dysmorphic presentation or fixed unrealistic expectations
  • Alopecia areata in an active phase
  • Under 18 years

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Age under 25 — counsel on future progression and the need for medical therapy
  • Smoking — significantly impairs graft survival; advise cessation 2 weeks before and after
  • Diffuse unpatterned alopecia — poor donor quality
  • Untreated thyroid disorder or severe anaemia
  • Isotretinoin within 6 months
  • Client not willing to take medical therapy to protect native hair
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Donor assessmentDensity per cm², scalp laxity and Norwood/Ludwig grade documented before booking
Graft numbersPlanned and agreed in writing at consultation; actual count recorded at the end of surgery
AnaesthesiaLocal (tumescent). Full monitoring and emergency kit in theatre

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Consultation
Surgeon assesses donor density, scalp laxity, Norwood/Ludwig grade and family pattern. Trichoscopy. Photograph from standard angles. Agree the graft plan and hairline in writing.
2
Pre-operative screen
Bloods — CBC, blood sugar, HbA1c, viral markers, coagulation profile. BP check. Physician clearance where indicated.
3
Consent and booking
Signed surgical consent covering shedding, final result timing, graft survival variability, scarring, numbness and the possibility of a second session. Booking card completed.
4
Pre-operative instructions
No alcohol 3 days before. No smoking 2 weeks before. Stop specified blood thinners per the surgeon. Wash hair the morning of surgery. Eat a normal breakfast. Wear a front-open shirt.
5
Hairline design
Designed with the client sitting upright, agreed and photographed before any incision.
6
Donor extraction
Local anaesthesia. FUE punch extraction from the permanent donor zone. Grafts placed immediately in the holding solution.
7
Recipient site creation
Sites created at the correct angle, direction and density per the design.
8
Implantation
Grafts implanted with minimum trauma and minimum out-of-body time. Count recorded.
9
Dressing and discharge
Dressing applied. Post-operative medication dispensed. Detailed written aftercare and the Day 1 wash appointment given.
10
Follow-up
Day 1 supervised wash. Reviews at Day 7, Day 15, Month 3, Month 6 and Month 12 with standardised photographs at each.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Graft out-of-body time is the single biggest controllable factor in survival — minimise it
  • Any client instability — BP, sugar, vasovagal — stops the procedure until resolved
  • Donor over-harvesting causes permanent visible thinning; stay within the assessed safe zone

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Post-operative medication dispensed and explained
  • Written aftercare handed over and read back
  • Day 1 wash appointment booked
  • Emergency contact number given

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Sleep with the head elevated at 45° for the first 7 nights
  • Attend the Day 1 supervised wash
  • Wash exactly as demonstrated from Day 2 — gently, no rubbing
  • Take all prescribed medication including antibiotics and anti-inflammatories
  • Expect swelling of the forehead around Day 2–4 — it settles
  • Expect the transplanted hair to SHED at 2–4 weeks — this is normal and expected
  • Be patient: regrowth starts at 3–4 months, final result at 12–18 months
  • Continue medical therapy to protect your native hair
  • Report fever, spreading redness, pus or heavy bleeding immediately

Avoid this

  • Do not touch, scratch or pick the grafts or scabs
  • No hat, helmet or anything touching the grafts for 7 days unless advised
  • No smoking for 2 weeks — it directly reduces graft survival
  • No alcohol for 1 week
  • No gym, swimming, sauna or heavy sweating for 3 weeks
  • No direct sun on the scalp for 4 weeks
  • No hair colour or chemical treatment for 4 weeks
  • Do not sleep face-down

  • Client under 25 with an aggressive progressing pattern and no medical therapy
  • Uncontrolled blood sugar or BP on the day of surgery
  • Hairline agreed verbally but not photographed and signed
  • Graft holding solution temperature or time not being monitored
  • Client actively smoking and unwilling to stop

1.0What this treatment is

A custom-made hair system fitted to the scalp that provides immediate, complete coverage for clients who are not candidates for transplant or who want an instant result.

The mechanism

A base of lace, skin or a hybrid material is templated to the client's scalp and ventilated with human hair matched for colour, texture, density and curl. It is attached with medical adhesive, tape or clips and serviced regularly as the natural scalp oils break down the bond.

Demonstrate home care, washing, sleeping and product use. Give the written care card.
7
Service booking
Book the first service at 3–4 weeks and explain the ongoing schedule.
8
Documentation
System specification, base type, attachment method, service schedule in ERP. Photograph the finished result.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Any scalp redness or irritation during fitting = stop and reassess adhesive choice
  • Never fit over an inflamed or broken scalp

  • First service booked

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Use only the recommended shampoo and products
  • Pat dry, do not rub
  • Report any itching, redness or rash under the base immediately

Avoid this

  • Do not attempt to remove the bond yourself with solvent
  • No harsh scrubbing of the base
  • Do not skip servicing — the bond degrades and the scalp underneath suffers
  • No excessive heat styling on the base

Body Composition Analysis (BCA / InBody)

BCA · InBody Composition Analysis · Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis
Session time5–10 minutesCourseBaseline, then every 4 weeks through a programmeIntervalEvery 4 weeksResults seenImmediate reportPerformed byTrained front office or therapist

1.0What this treatment is

A body composition measurement that separates weight into fat mass, muscle mass, visceral fat and body water — the baseline for every slimming programme.

The mechanism

Bioelectrical impedance sends a low, safe electrical current through the body. Lean tissue conducts easily because of its water content; fat resists. The resistance profile is converted into fat mass, skeletal muscle mass, visceral fat level and total body water.

Equipment used

BCA Machine · Height Machine · Weight Machine

Reference SOP

SOP-SLM-002 §2 Step 1

2.0What it treats

  • Baseline before any slimming programme
  • 4-weekly progress tracking
  • GLP-1 programme monitoring — protecting lean mass is the whole point
  • Demonstrating fat loss when scale weight has not moved

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • General. Adults on any slimming, nutrition or GLP-1 programme
  • Preparation. Empty bladder, no heavy meal or exercise in the previous 2 hours, no alcohol in 24 hours
  • Consistency. Same time of day, same conditions each time — otherwise the comparison is meaningless

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Pregnancy
  • Cardiac pacemaker or implanted electronic device — bioimpedance is contraindicated

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Significant oedema or fluid retention — results will be distorted
  • Dialysis clients
  • Recent heavy exercise or large meal — reschedule
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
Standard conditionsSame time of day, empty bladder, no meal or exercise in the previous 2 hours
Recorded metricsWeight, BMI, fat mass, skeletal muscle mass, visceral fat level, total body water
CircumferenceAbdomen at the umbilicus, waist at the narrowest point, hips, thighs, upper arms — standardised tension tape
Photography4-angle standardised photographs at baseline and every 4 weeks

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Screen
Confirm no pacemaker and not pregnant. Confirm preparation conditions were met.
2
Standardise
Remove shoes, socks and heavy jewellery. Same clothing weight standard each time.
3
Measure
Run the analysis per the machine protocol with correct hand and foot electrode contact.
4
Circumference
Take standardised tape measurements at the same anatomical points.
5
Photograph
4 angles — anterior, posterior, left lateral, right lateral — in the fixed-lighting photo booth.
6
Explain
Walk the client through fat mass vs muscle mass. Set the expectation that scale weight alone is a poor measure.
7
Documentation
Store the report, measurements and photographs in the ERP client record.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Pacemaker disclosed = do not run the analysis
  • Poor electrode contact gives a false reading — recheck rather than accept it

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Report explained and printed
  • Next BCA booked at 4 weeks

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Come at the same time of day for every analysis
  • Empty your bladder before the test
  • Avoid heavy meals and exercise for 2 hours before

Avoid this

  • No alcohol in the 24 hours before
  • Do not compare readings taken under different conditions

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
None expected—Non-invasive. No known adverse effects when contraindications are respected.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Pacemaker or implanted device disclosed
  • Client pregnant
  • Reading taken under non-standard conditions and then compared to baseline

Trichoscopy & Skin Analysis

E-Scope Trichoscopy · Skin Analyzer · Digital Scalp Analysis
Session time15–20 minutesCourseBaseline, then every 3 months through a programmeIntervalEvery 3 monthsResults seenImmediate on-screen reportPerformed byTrained therapist or doctor

1.0What this treatment is

Magnified digital imaging of the scalp or skin that shows follicle density, miniaturisation, scalp condition, pore size, pigmentation and hydration — turning a subjective consultation into a documented baseline.

The mechanism

A high-magnification camera with polarised and UV light modes images the scalp or skin surface and sub-surface. Follicle counts, hair shaft diameter variation, sebum, pigment distribution and hydration are read from the images and compared over time.

Equipment used

E-Scope (Hair) · E-Scope (Skin) · Skin analyzer · Magnifying lamp / derma camera

Reference SOP

Cluster Dermat Training Programme — Visit 1 & 3 modules

2.0What it treats

  • Baseline before any hair loss programme
  • Distinguishing pattern hair loss from telogen effluvium
  • Scalp condition assessment — dandruff, seborrhoea, folliculitis
  • Skin baseline — pores, pigment, hydration, sebum
  • Documenting progress at 3-month intervals

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • General. Any client starting a hair or skin programme
  • Preparation. Scalp not oiled on the day; skin without makeup for skin analysis

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Active weeping or infected lesion — image but do not press the probe onto it

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Heavy oil or product in the hair on the day — reschedule or wash first for a usable image
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

1
Prepare
Confirm no oil or product. Disinfect the probe tip.
2

Vertex, mid-scalp, frontal and occipital donor for hair. Forehead, cheeks, nose and chin for skin.

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Come without makeup for skin analysis

LIFE RISE & Nutrition

Clinical Nutrition & LIFE RISE Programme

LIFE RISE · Customised Diet Plan · Dietician Consultation · Online Nutrition Programme
Session time45–60 minutes for the first consultation; 20–30 minutes for reviewsCourseOngoing programme with structured reviewsIntervalWeekly to monthly depending on plan tierResults seenMeasured against body composition, not scale weight alonePerformed byQualified dietician. Medical decisions and prescriptions: doctor only.

1.0What this treatment is

A structured, medically supervised nutrition programme that prioritises fat loss while actively protecting lean muscle — delivered in clinic or online, alone or alongside a clinical treatment plan.

The mechanism

Total Daily Energy Expenditure is calculated from weight, height, age, gender and activity level. A safe, progressive caloric deficit is set with protein held high to preserve lean mass. Behaviour change — food logging, mindful eating, meal structure — is the part that determines whether the result lasts.

Equipment used

BCA Machine · InBody · online platform

Reference SOP

LIFE RISE Programme Book 1 — Master SOP · SOP-SLM-002 §3

2.0What it treats

  • Weight loss and fat loss programmes
  • Support alongside GLP-1 therapy — protein intake is mandatory, not optional
  • Post-treatment maintenance
  • Metabolic risk — prediabetes, dyslipidaemia, PCOS
  • Skin and hair conditions with a nutritional driver
  • Weight maintenance after a programme completes

3.0Who can and cannot be treated

The left column is what a suitable candidate looks like. The right column stops the session outright. Screen against both before every session, not only the first.

✓Eligible — suitable candidate

  • General. Adults on any slimming, GLP-1 or wellness programme
  • Baseline. BCA and, where indicated, a blood panel completed before the plan is written
  • Commitment. Willing to log food and attend reviews

✕Absolute — do not treat

  • Dieticians must NOT prescribe or adjust any medication — doctor only
  • Dieticians must NOT diagnose a medical condition
  • Dieticians must NOT advise on GLP-1 dosing or titration
  • Deficits below 1,200 kcal/day without medical supervision
  • Extended fasting beyond 12 hours without medical supervision

Relative contraindications — clearance required first

These do not rule the client out. They mean the doctor or dermatologist decides, in writing, before you proceed.

  • Pregnancy or breastfeeding — plan must be written with doctor involvement
  • Type 1 diabetes or insulin-treated Type 2 — doctor-supervised plan only
  • Chronic kidney disease — protein targets must be set by the physician
  • History of disordered eating — psychological support alongside, and no restrictive targets
  • Adolescents — growth-appropriate plans only, with guardian involvement
The therapist ruleWhen in doubt, do not treat. Call the Centre Manager or the in-house dermatologist. Treating an ineligible client is a serious clinical and legal risk. Stopping a session over a contraindication is doing the job correctly, and no one at LIFE is penalised for it.

4.0Parameters and settings

Starting reference points from the LIFE SOP. The treating clinician adjusts to skin response, tissue type and machine calibration — never upward beyond the stated ceiling.

Working parameters
ParameterSpecification
TDEECalculated from weight, height, age, gender and activity level. Documented in ERP
Caloric deficitSafe and progressive as determined by the doctor or nutritionist. Avoid below 1,200 kcal/day without medical supervision
ProteinMinimum 1.2 g per kg of reference body weight daily. 60–80 g minimum on GLP-1 therapy
CarbohydrateComplex, low-glycaemic sources only — fibre-rich vegetables, legumes, oats. Avoid refined sugars
FatsOmega-3 (fish oil, flaxseed) and monounsaturated (olive oil, avocado). Minimise saturated and trans fats
Meal frequency3–5 small, balanced meals per day. No extended fasting beyond 12 hours without supervision
Food loggingWeekly review of the client's food diary. Flag high-calorie or nutritionally deficient days

5.0Step-by-step protocol

1
Baseline assessment
Medical history, medications, allergies, food preferences, work pattern, cultural and religious dietary requirements. BCA and measurements. Blood panel where indicated.
2
Calculate and design
Calculate TDEE. Set the deficit, protein floor and macro split. Build a plan the client can actually follow — Indian household food, not imported ingredients.
3
Explain the plan
Walk through the plan with the client. Confirm they can source and cook it. Adjust rather than hand over a plan they will abandon in a week.
4
Behavioural setup
Set up food logging. Identify emotional eating triggers — stress, boredom, sleep deprivation. Agree the review rhythm.
5
Weekly review
Review the food diary. Flag deficient days. Adjust in small steps.
6
4-weekly BCA
Repeat body composition. Judge progress on fat mass and muscle mass, not scale weight.
7
Escalate where required
Any red flag — see below — goes to the doctor. Dieticians do not manage medical issues.
8
Maintenance phase
Structured transition to maintenance calories with continued monitoring. This is where most programmes fail — plan it deliberately.
Watch continuously — these stop the session
  • Dieticians work strictly within scope — no diagnosis, no prescription, no dose advice
  • Any client losing weight faster than planned, or reporting dizziness, palpitations or fainting, goes to the doctor
  • Any sign of disordered eating stops the restrictive plan and triggers a doctor referral

Before the client leaves the chair

  • Written plan issued
  • Food logging set up
  • Next review booked

6.0What the client is told

Say it, then hand over the printed sheet. A client who does not follow aftercare will not get the result — and will believe the treatment failed.

Do this

  • Log everything you eat — accuracy matters more than perfection
  • Hit your protein target every day, especially on GLP-1 therapy
  • Include strength training to protect muscle
  • Attend your reviews and your 4-weekly BCA
  • Tell the clinic about any new medication or medical diagnosis

Avoid this

  • Do not skip meals to speed up results
  • Do not go below the calorie floor set for you
  • Do not change your GLP-1 dose based on diet advice — that is the doctor's decision only
  • Do not judge progress on the scale alone

7.0Adverse events and immediate action

Graded response
EventSeverityImmediate action
Fatigue or dizzinessModerate (P3)Review calorie floor and hydration. Doctor referral if it persists. Document.
Rapid or excessive weight lossModerate (P3)Doctor review. Reassess the deficit. Document.
Signs of disordered eatingSerious (P2)Stop the restrictive plan. Doctor referral. Psychological support. Escalate to the LIFE RISE Lead. Document.
Hair fall during weight lossModerate (P3)Check protein, ferritin, Vitamin D and thyroid. Doctor referral. Common with rapid loss — counsel at the start so it is never a surprise.

Red flags — stop and escalate

  • Dietician advising on medication or GLP-1 dosing — strictly out of scope
  • Any plan below 1,200 kcal/day without medical supervision
  • Client showing signs of disordered eating
  • Client with unexplained rapid weight loss
  • Client reporting fainting, palpitations or chest pain
  • Pregnancy disclosed on a restrictive plan
